f:198484: Shot in and around London in the very months the novel is set.
f:28dayslater: Emptied central London at dawn for minutes at a time, shooting on consumer digital cameras.
f:400blows: A boy runs away to the sea. Its director had been banned from the festival as a critic the year before.
f:42ndst: The backstage musical, with overhead numbers by a former army drill instructor.
f:4months: The first Romanian Palme; about an illegal abortion in 1987 Bucharest, shot in long takes.
f:aan: Among the first Indian films in colour, released across Europe.
f:abrightersummerday91: Four hours long, with a cast of a hundred unknowns.
f:abyss: A scandalously erotic dance made its lead Europe’s first film star overnight.
f:aceinhole: A reporter keeps a trapped man underground to stretch out his story. Too bleak for audiences at the time.
f:acesgoplaces: Hong Kong’s biggest box-office hit to that date.
f:achhut: A love story across caste lines.
f:achmed: The oldest surviving animated feature, made from hand-cut silhouettes over three years.
f:acrossspiderverse: Every universe drawn in its own style, from watercolour to punk collage; about a thousand artists worked on it, and some described the schedule as punishing.
f:actofkilling: Indonesian death-squad leaders re-enact their killings as scenes from their favourite movie genres.
f:adaptation: Its writer credited his fictional twin brother, who was nominated for an Oscar.
f:aelita: Remembered for its angular Constructivist Martian costumes and sets.
f:affairremember: Its director remade his own 1939 film.
f:africanqueen: Shot on location in Africa, where most of the crew fell ill except the two who drank only whisky.
f:aftershock10: A mother must choose which of her twins to save from the 1976 Tangshan earthquake; the first Chinese IMAX film.
f:aftersun: A daughter remembers a Turkish package holiday with her young father through old camcorder footage; a first feature that critics ranked among the decade’s best.
f:agedor: A riot at its premiere got it banned; it stayed out of circulation for nearly fifty years.
f:agoodyear_x: The highest-grossing film ever in Britain until then.
f:aguirre: Conquistadors drift down the Amazon on rafts; its director reportedly threatened his star with a rifle to keep him on set.
f:ahiesta: The breakthrough of a comic whose tangled speech became a national treasure.
f:aimlessbullet: Banned soon after release; often voted the greatest Korean film.
f:airplane: Largely the plot of a 1957 airline drama, played dead straight by actors known for serious roles. "And don’t call me Shirley."
f:aiye: A founding father of Nigerian theatre’s first film: witchcraft and a herbalist’s battle, a huge Yoruba hit.
f:ajaniogun: A Yoruba travelling-theatre star’s first feature; it launched a wave of Yoruba cinema.
f:akira: Neo-Tokyo, 2019. Some 160,000 cels, and dialogue recorded before animation, rare in Japan.
f:aladdin: Its genie star recorded hours of improvised material for union scale, then fell out with the studio over marketing.
f:alamara: India’s first sound film, with seven songs. No print is known to survive.
f:alamo: Its star directed and put his own money into it.
f:alcarras: A family’s last peach harvest before their orchard becomes a solar farm, played by non-actors from the region.
f:alexandriawhy: The first of its director’s autobiographical films: a boy in wartime Alexandria who wants to go to Hollywood.
f:alfie: Its lead talks straight to camera.
f:algiers: Staged so realistically it opened with a notice that no newsreel footage was used. Banned in France for years; studied later by militaries.
f:alice03: The first film version of the book, running about twelve minutes.
f:alice88: Wonderland as a drawer of stuffed animals, sawdust and animated meat.
f:alien: "In space no one can hear you scream." The cast were not told exactly what would burst from the chest.
f:aliens: Its lead earned a rare acting nomination for a genre film.
f:alifear: A Munich cleaning lady in her sixties marries a younger Moroccan worker; a remake in spirit of a 1955 Hollywood melodrama.
f:allabouteve: A record fourteen nominations for a backstage story about an ambitious understudy.
f:allquiet: An anti-war classic from a German novel, banned in Germany after the Nazis disrupted its screenings.
f:allquiet22: The first German-language adaptation of the novel won four Oscars, including for a score built on a three-note harmonium blast.
f:allthatjazz: Its director staged his own death as a musical number, eight years before it happened.
f:allthebeauty: A photographer’s life and her campaign against the family that sold the painkiller that almost killed her.
f:allweimagine: Two nurses in monsoon Mumbai, then a trip to the coast. The first Indian film in the main Cannes competition in thirty years, and it won the second prize.
f:almostfamous: Based on its director touring with bands for a rock magazine at fifteen.
f:alphaville: A science-fiction city shot in real 1960s Paris with no special effects.
f:alwaysforpleasure: Mardi Gras, second lines, red beans and crawfish in New Orleans, filmed by a documentarian of American food and music.
f:amadeus: Its émigré director went back to shoot in communist Prague, whose candlelit opera house Mozart himself had conducted in.
f:amarakbar: Three brothers separated as children are raised Hindu, Muslim and Christian.
f:ambersons: The studio cut about forty minutes and added a happier ending while its director was in Brazil; the lost footage is film history’s holy grail.
f:amelie: Its director digitally cleaned Montmartre of graffiti and litter.
f:americangraffiti: One night of cruising in 1962; made for under $800,000, it became one of the most profitable films ever.
f:americanhistoryx: Its director fought to have his name taken off it after its star recut it.
f:americanpsycho: A banker’s killing spree as satire of eighties excess; its studio briefly replaced its director and star with Leonardo DiCaprio before relenting.
f:americansplendor: A Cleveland file clerk’s comics, with the real Harvey Pekar commenting between scenes played by an actor.
f:anand: A dying man who refuses to be sad; its young co-star would soon eclipse the lead.
f:anastasia: Its lead’s comeback after years of scandal in America.
f:anatomyfall: A writer is tried for her husband’s death; the case turns on the testimony of their partially sighted son and on the dog, who won an unofficial prize at the festival.
f:anchorsaweigh: Its lead dances with an animated mouse.
f:aneducation: A sixteen-year-old in 1961 Twickenham is courted by a charming older man; from a memoir, adapted by a novelist.
f:angelmytable: Janet Frame’s autobiography, made for television and released to cinemas.
f:animalhouse: A humour magazine’s college satire, shot at the University of Oregon; toga parties swept campuses.
f:ankur: A landlord’s son and a Dalit servant woman; its director had made hundreds of ad films first.
f:annachristie: Sold with two words about its star: she talks.
f:anniehall: Beat the space opera for the top prize; its director stayed in New York to play clarinet at his usual pub.
f:anora: A Brooklyn stripper marries an oligarch’s son in Las Vegas; his family’s fixers come to undo it. Made for $6 million, its director won four Oscars in a night, a record for one person on one film.
f:anotherround: Four teachers test the theory that humans are born half a drink short; ends in a dance by the harbour.
f:anouslaliberte: Its assembly-line satire was later said to resemble a 1936 comedy by a famous tramp.
f:anyonebutyou: Opened soft, then grew week after week, helping revive studio romantic comedy.
f:aotc: The first major film shot entirely on digital video.
f:apartment: An office clerk lends his flat to his bosses for their affairs.
f:apocalypsenow: Shot for more than a year in the Philippines: a typhoon destroyed the sets and its lead had a heart attack. "My film is not about Vietnam. It is Vietnam."
f:apoet: A failed middle-aged poet in Medellín finds a talented teenage girl to mentor and makes a mess of it. Its lead is a schoolteacher, not an actor.
f:apollo11: Built entirely from newly found 65mm NASA footage and eleven thousand hours of audio; no narration.
f:apollo13: Its weightless scenes were filmed in real zero gravity aboard NASA’s ‘vomit comet’ in 25-second bursts.
f:apostol: The world’s first animated feature, a political satire. Its only print was destroyed in a fire.
f:applause: Set the early talkie camera free when most films were stuck in soundproof booths.
f:apursansar: The end of a trilogy, and the debut of an actor who appeared in fourteen of his director’s films.
f:arabianknights: Its prize category was awarded only once.
f:aradhana: Made its lead the first "superstar" of Hindi cinema.
f:argentina1985: The prosecutors who put the generals of the dictatorship on trial.
f:argo: The real CIA ruse used a fake science-fiction film to smuggle six diplomats out of Tehran.
f:arirang: A quiet act of resistance under colonial rule and the most beloved Korean film of its era; now lost.
f:armyshadows: Barely released in America until 2006, when it topped critics’ year-end lists.
f:arne: Ends with a funeral procession across the sea ice.
f:around80: Its showman producer invented the word “cameo” for its star walk-ons.
f:arroseur: A boy steps on a hose, a gardener gets drenched: the first known staged film comedy.
f:ascent: Two partisans in the Belarusian snow, one a martyr, one a collaborator. Its director died in a car crash two years later.
f:aseparation: A divorce, a caretaker and a fall on the stairs; every character is partly right.
f:aserious: A physics professor in 1967 Minnesota seeks answers from three rabbis; the brothers’ most autobiographical film, opening with a Yiddish folk tale.
f:asgoodasitgets: The last film to win both lead acting Oscars until years later; its dog had six understudies.
f:ashanisanket: The Bengal famine of 1943 arrives in a village.
f:asphaltjungle: The template for the heist film.
f:astearsgoby: A screenwriter’s debut as director, a Mong Kok triad story in smeared neon.
f:asteroidcity: A desert town of the 1950s, built life-size in a Spanish field.
f:atalante: A newlywed couple on a river barge. Its director was dying during the shoot and never saw it properly released.
f:athena: A riot on a housing estate, told in long unbroken takes.
f:atlantics: Young construction workers lost at sea return to haunt Dakar; the first Black woman in competition at Cannes.
f:atonement: Its five-minute Dunkirk beach shot used a thousand extras and had to be finished before the tide came in.
f:attackblock: South London teenagers fight furry black aliens with fireworks and a samurai sword.
f:aurevoirenfants: Its director’s own childhood: a Catholic boarding school hiding Jewish boys in 1944.
f:automovil: Based on a real Mexico City gang, and said to include footage of their actual execution.
f:autumnsonata: The only time the two Bergmans worked together; her last cinema role.
f:avatar: Written in 1994 and shelved until the technology existed; became the highest-grossing film in history and restarted 3D.
f:avengers12: Four solo franchises collided in one film, and the cinematic universe became the business model of Hollywood.
f:aviator: Its colour mimics two-strip then three-strip Technicolor as the years pass.
f:avventura: A woman vanishes on an island and is never found. Booed at the screening, then defended in an open letter by filmmakers.
f:awaara: A tramp hero, a dream sequence and a song that became famous from Moscow to Istanbul.
f:awfultruth: Its director improvised scenes on set, and its male lead found his screen persona.
f:awomanundertheinfl74: Self-distributed, the reels driven round to cinemas by the filmmakers themselves.
f:baazi51: The first film of a young choreographer turned director, made for his friend's company.
f:baazigar: Made a television actor a star by letting him play the murderer.
f:babe: Forty-eight piglets played the lead, because piglets grow too fast.
f:babettesfeast: A French refugee cook spends her lottery winnings on one dinner for a pious Jutland village.
f:babybring: A leopard, a dinosaur bone and a flop so costly its lead bought out her studio contract.
f:babyface33: Its frankness helped bring in the censorship code the following year.
f:babyjane: Two ageing stars who loathed each other, playing sisters who loathe each other.
f:backrooms: Its director made the found-footage web series it is based on as a teenager, and was barely out of his teens when the film was released.
f:backtofuture: Its original lead was replaced five weeks into shooting; the new one was also filming a sitcom by day.
f:badtaste: Aliens harvesting humans for fast food, made over four years of weekends by a photo-engraver in his twenties.
f:badtiming80: Its own distributor called it a sick film made by sick people for sick people.
f:badtrip: A hidden-camera road-trip comedy: everyone but the three leads is a real, unsuspecting member of the public.
f:bahubali1: The most expensive Indian film of its day, shot in Telugu and Tamil at once.
f:bakerswife: A Provençal village goes without bread when the baker’s wife runs off: vintage Pagnol.
f:balthazar: The life of a donkey, and the cruelty of the people around him.
f:banditqueen: Its real subject sued to stop it, then became an MP.
f:banshees: On an Irish island in 1923 one friend simply stops liking the other; a donkey stole several scenes.
f:barbie: A doll leaves her pink world for the real one. It opened the same day as a three-hour film about the atomic bomb, and audiences turned the double bill into an event; the sets used so much pink paint that a supplier ran short.
f:barrylyndon: Interiors lit only by candles, shot through lenses built for NASA.
f:barsaat: A huge musical hit that paid for its young director’s new studio.
f:barton: Written in three weeks to escape writer’s block on another script; won three top prizes at Cannes, after which the rules were changed.
f:bashu: A dark-skinned boy from the war-torn south finds refuge with a northern mother who can’t understand his language; shelved for three years.
f:basicinstinct: Its writer was paid a record $3 million for the script.
f:batman89: Fans sent some 50,000 letters protesting the casting of a comic actor; its villain took a share of the gross and made a fortune.
f:batmanreturns: McDonald’s pulled its Happy Meal tie-in after parents complained the film was too dark.
f:battleroyale: Debated in the Japanese parliament before release.
f:battleshonor: Hiroshima yakuza after the bomb, shot handheld; five films in two years.
f:bayankomyowncountr84: Smuggled out of the country for its festival premiere.
f:beautravail: Foreign Legionnaires in Djibouti; ends with its star alone on a disco floor.
f:beautybeast91: The first animated film nominated for Best Picture; its lyricist died before it opened.
f:beforesunrise: One night in Vienna; its sequels followed at nine-year intervals.
f:beforethedevilknow07: Made at eighty-three, his last film.
f:belledejour: A cold bourgeois wife spends her afternoons working in a brothel, and her daydreams bleed into reality. Its director’s biggest commercial hit.
f:belleetbete: Living arms hold candelabras along the Beast’s corridors.
f:benhur25: The most expensive silent film ever made. Its chariot race is legendary, but the studio still lost money on it.
f:benhur59: A record eleven Academy prizes; its chariot race took months to shoot. It saved its studio.
f:berlinsym: One day in the life of a city, cut to rhythm.
f:bestgirl: Its star’s last silent film; she married her co-star years later.
f:bestyears: Three veterans come home. One was played by a real veteran who had lost both hands.
f:bethereorbesquare98: One of the first New Year comedies, a genre its director all but invented.
f:bettertomorrow: Young men copied its star’s long duster coat and matchstick; the start of "heroic bloodshed."
f:beudet: An early feminist film about a wife trapped in a provincial marriage.
f:beverlyhillscop: Written for a very different muscle star; its synth theme was everywhere.
f:bhuvanshome: A starchy railway official goes duck hunting in Gujarat; state-funded, it helped launch Indian parallel cinema.
f:bicyclethieves: A father and son search Rome for a stolen bicycle. Its director refused Hollywood money that would have meant a star in the lead.
f:big: The first film directed by a woman to gross over $100 million in America.
f:bigboss: Shot in Thailand; made its star a sensation across Asia overnight.
f:bigbusiness: A tit-for-tat escalation that destroys a house and a car.
f:bigfatgreek: Made for $5 million from a one-woman show; never reached number one in any week, yet became the highest-grossing romantic comedy ever.
f:bigheat: A pot of scalding coffee thrown in a woman’s face made it notorious.
f:biglebowski: A modest flop that spawned a festival, a religion and endless White Russians.
f:bignight: Two Italian brothers stake their failing restaurant on one feast; ends with a wordless five-minute take of an omelette being made.
f:bigparade: The studio’s biggest silent-era hit, made for a fraction of what it earned.
f:bigsleep: So confusing that nobody, reportedly including the novelist, could say who killed the chauffeur.
f:bigtrail: Shot in an early widescreen process few cinemas could show. Its flop sent its new star to a decade of B-westerns.
f:billyjack: Its star-director won it back from the studio and re-released it with saturation TV ads, a strategy the majors soon copied.
f:birdman: Staged and cut to look like one continuous take through a Broadway theatre.
f:birds: Its lead spent a week having live birds thrown at her for one scene.
f:birth: A landmark of film technique and of racist propaganda: it glorified the Ku Klux Klan, drew NAACP protests, and fuelled the Klan’s revival.
f:bitterrice: Neorealism meets sex appeal in the rice fields; a worldwide hit.
f:blackchristmas: A sorority house, obscene phone calls from inside the house, and a killer never unmasked.
f:blackgirl66: Often called the first feature by a sub-Saharan African director.
f:blackmail: Britain’s first talkie. Its lead’s accent was replaced live, by an actress speaking her lines just off camera.
f:blacknarcissus: Nuns in a Himalayan palace, entirely filmed in an English studio with painted mountains. Its colour photography won an Academy prize.
f:blackorpheus: A myth retold during Rio’s carnival; its bossa nova score spread the genre worldwide.
f:blackpanther: The first superhero film nominated for Best Picture; its costume and design leads became the first Black winners in their categories.
f:blackpirate: An early feature shot entirely in colour.
f:blacksunday: Banned in Britain for eight years.
f:bladerunner: A modest hit, then the most influential science-fiction look of its era; seven different cuts exist. "Tears in rain" was partly written by its replicant actor.
f:bladerunner2049: Its cinematographer finally won the Oscar on his fourteenth nomination.
f:blairwitch: Made for about $60,000; its website convinced many that the footage was real.
f:blazingsaddles: A Black sheriff in a racist frontier town; its campfire scene was a first.
f:blimp: Forty years of an English officer’s life, with a sympathetic German friend. Churchill tried to stop it being made.
f:blindhusbands19: He talked his way into directing it by offering to write and star for almost nothing.
f:blithespirit: A novelist’s dead first wife is summoned by a medium and refuses to leave. From a stage comedy that ran through the war.
f:bloke: From a bestselling book of verse in Australian slang; a local classic.
f:bloodsand: Its editor intercut real bullfight footage so well she was soon given films to direct.
f:bloodsimple: The brothers shot a trailer to raise money door to door in Minneapolis.
f:blowup: A photographer thinks he has captured a murder in a park. Released without a production-code seal and a hit anyway.
f:bluangel: Made in German and English versions; it launched its female lead to Hollywood.
f:bluesbrothers: Crashed a record number of police cars, some 103.
f:bluevelvet: A severed ear in a suburban field, and the rot beneath the white picket fences.
f:bluewarmest: The jury gave the Palme to the director and both actresses, the first time actors shared it.
f:boatpeople: A Japanese photographer in postwar Vietnam; shot in China’s Hainan island.
f:bobby73: A teen romance made to pay off its director’s debts; it did.
f:bodhidharma: A painting professor made it alone over several years, shooting, editing and directing himself.
f:bodyguard: Written in the 1970s for Steve McQueen and Diana Ross; its soundtrack became the best-selling of all time.
f:bodysoul: The screen debut of a singer and actor who became one of the great voices of the century.
f:bonnieclyde: Panned, pulled, re-released after critics recanted: the film that announced New Hollywood.
f:boonmee: A dying man in the northeast is visited by the ghost of his wife and his son, who has become a red-eyed monkey spirit.
f:borat: Most of its subjects did not know it was a comedy; several sued.
f:bornbut: Two boys discover their father is not the most important man in the world.
f:boyheron: Released in Japan with no trailer, no poster beyond a single drawing, and no advance publicity at all.
f:boyhood: Filmed a few days each year for twelve years as its young lead grew up.
f:boyzhood: Its director was twenty-three, the youngest nominee for Best Director and the first Black one.
f:brandedtokill: The number-three hitman in Japan, obsessed with the smell of boiling rice. Its studio fired the director for making it incomprehensible; students protested, he sued, and was blacklisted for ten years.
f:braveheart: Shot in Ireland with members of the Irish Army Reserve as both armies.
f:brazil85: Its studio wanted a happy ending; its director took out a trade-paper ad asking its chairman when he would release it.
f:breakermorant: Three Australian officers court-martialled by the British during the Boer War. "Shoot straight, you bastards. Don’t make a mess of it!"
f:breakfastclub: Five teenagers in Saturday detention, shot in a gym in a Chicago suburb.
f:breakingnews: Opens with a seven-minute unbroken shootout down a whole street; the police turn a siege into live television.
f:breakingwaves: Shot handheld on 35mm, transferred to video and back to film to give its images a strange colour.
f:breathless: A petty crook and an American girl selling papers on the Champs-Élysées. Its jump cuts began as a way to shorten the film.
f:briefencounter: An affair that never quite happens, in a railway station tea room.
f:brighteyes34: She sings about a lollipop on an aeroplane; she was six.
f:broadwaymelody: The first talkie and the first musical to win the top Academy prize, and the top film of 1929.
f:brokeback: Lost Best Picture in one of the most-discussed upsets in Oscar history.
f:brokenbarrier: A romance across the Māori and Pākehā divide; New Zealand’s only feature for years.
f:bronxtale: Its writer turned down $1 million for the rights to his one-man play unless he could play the gangster Sonny.
f:brutalist: A three-and-a-half-hour epic, with an intermission, shot on VistaVision for under $10 million.
f:bulletsfly: A bandit impersonates a county governor in 1920s Sichuan; the most-quoted Chinese comedy of the decade.
f:bullitt: A ten-minute car chase over San Francisco’s hills; its star did some of the driving himself.
f:butchcassidy: Ends on a freeze-frame as the outlaws run into Bolivian gunfire.
f:butterfield: Its lead called it the worst film she ever made; many thought her prize was a sympathy vote after a near-fatal illness.
f:byebyebrasil: A travelling circus crosses a Brazil being rewired by television.
f:cabaret: Won eight Academy prizes yet lost Best Picture to a gangster saga.
f:cabiria: Its moving-camera shots and colossal sets influenced Hollywood’s epics, and its strongman got a series of his own.
f:caesarandcleopatra45: The most expensive British film yet made, with sand shipped to Egypt for the desert.
f:cageauxfolles: For years the most successful foreign-language film ever released in America.
f:cairostation: A newspaper seller’s obsession; its director played the lead. Audiences rejected it; it is now a classic of Arab cinema.
f:caligari: Painted, crooked sets and a twist ending: the founding work of German Expressionism.
f:camerabuff: A factory worker buys a camera to film his baby and ends up filming his factory’s lies.
f:cameraman: The first film after its star lost his independence to a big studio.
f:cangaceiro: A Brazilian bandit western that won a prize on the Riviera and toured the world.
f:cannibalholocaust: Its director was charged over rumours his actors had been killed; he produced them in court.
f:canoa: Recreates the 1968 lynching of university workers by villagers stirred up by their priest.
f:capefear91: A remake that reused the original’s Bernard Herrmann score, rearranged by Elmer Bernstein.
f:captainblood: Turned two unknowns into swashbuckling stars.
f:capturingfriedmans: Started as a film about birthday-party clowns in New York; one clown’s family had filmed itself during a child-abuse investigation.
f:carmen15: An opera star in a silent film, and the year’s second-biggest hit.
f:carnavalfogo: A classic of the carnival-comedy genre that ruled Brazilian box offices.
f:carnivalnight: A New Year’s musical comedy seen by nearly fifty million people.
f:carrie: The first adaptation of a novel by a young Maine schoolteacher who would become the most filmed author alive.
f:carryonsergeant: The first of thirty cheap, cheeky comedies that ran for twenty years.
f:casablanca: An assembly-line studio picture with a script rewritten during filming, and possibly the most beloved film ever made.
f:casinoroyale: Its blond lead was mocked by a website before release; a parkour free-runner did his own crane chase.
f:castaway: Production stopped for a year so its star could lose fifty pounds; the director made another film in the gap.
f:castlepurity: A father locks his family in their house for eighteen years; from a real case.
f:catballou: Its lead won for playing a drunk gunfighter and his evil twin, and thanked a horse.
f:catcanary: The template for every old-dark-house mystery.
f:catpeople: Made for about $134,000 with the monster never shown. It was a hit that kept its studio afloat.
f:caucasus: The biggest Soviet film of 1967, seen by over 76 million people.
f:ceddo: Banned in Senegal for years, officially over the spelling of its title.
f:cendrillon: A fairy tale told in twenty tableaux, long for its day.
f:cerclerouge: A near-silent 25-minute jewel heist; its comic star’s last role, and a straight one.
f:cesar36: The third of the waterfront trilogy, and the only one he directed himself.
f:chaingang: Based on a real escapee’s memoir; its exposé helped reform Georgia’s prison camps.
f:chandralekha: The most expensive Indian film of its time, famous for a drum dance performed atop giant drums.
f:chapaev: A civil-war hero film seen by tens of millions; its hero became the subject of endless Soviet jokes.
f:chariotsfire: Its writer accepted with "The British are coming!"; the synth theme became the sound of slow motion.
f:charulata: Its director called it the film he would make the same way again.
f:cheat: Its deep shadows made dramatic lighting fashionable.
f:chienandalou: Opens with a razor and an eye. Its director kept stones in his pockets at the premiere in case the audience turned on him.
f:children: A film about birth control and abortion that became one of Universal’s biggest hits of the year.
f:childrenmen: Its car ambush and battle were each a single continuous shot; blood spattered on the lens and they kept rolling.
f:childrenparadise: Made under the Occupation, with some crew working in secret; its star was jailed after the Liberation.
f:chimes: Falstaff’s story stitched from five Shakespeare plays, shot in Spain on a shoestring. Its battle scene was cut from a few hundred extras to look like thousands. Barely distributed for decades.
f:chinatown: "Forget it, Jake, it’s Chinatown." Its director overruled the writer’s hopeful ending; Los Angeles water politics as noir.
f:chintamani: The first Tamil film to run for a year.
f:chungking: Shot in two months while its director was stuck editing a martial arts epic; Quentin Tarantino’s first distribution release.
f:churchillsisland: The first documentary to win an Academy prize, from Canada’s new national film board.
f:cimarron: Won the top prize and still lost money.
f:cinderella50: A make-or-break film for a studio in debt after the war; it made it.
f:cinemaparadiso: Flopped in Italy at full length; a shorter cut conquered the world. The censor’s kisses spliced together.
f:circus: Its maker received a special honour at the first Academy ceremony for writing, acting, directing and producing it.
f:citizenkane: A newspaper tycoon’s life told in fragments. The real tycoon it resembled tried to have it destroyed; it lost money and topped critics’ polls for half a century.
f:citygirl30: Cut and part-reshot by the studio without him.
f:citygod: Cast almost entirely from young people in Rio’s favelas, who workshopped the scenes for months.
f:citylights: A silent film three years into the talkies, and the top film of 1931. Its final close-up is one of cinema’s greatest.
f:cityofsadness: The first film to depict the 1947 massacre known as February 28, possible only after martial law ended in 1987.
f:citysl: Its supporting winner did one-armed push-ups at the Oscars.
f:civilwar24: The most expensive film its studio had made.
f:cleo: A singer awaits a medical diagnosis, almost in real time.
f:cleopatra63: The top film of 1963 and still a disaster: the most expensive film ever made at the time nearly bankrupted its studio. Its stars’ affair made headlines worldwide.
f:clerks: Made for $27,575 on credit cards at the convenience store where its director worked; shot at night after closing.
f:clockwork: Its director withdrew it from British cinemas himself after threats and copycat claims; it stayed unseen there until his death.
f:closeencounters: Five notes, a mountain sculpted from mashed potatoes, and a French director playing a scientist.
f:closeup: A man arrested for impersonating a famous director plays himself in the reconstruction; the real director turns up at the end.
f:cloudatlas12: Co-directed with a German director; each half of the team shot its own stories.
f:cloudcapped: A refugee family after partition; its heroine’s last cry is one of Indian cinema’s great moments.
f:cloverfield08: Sold on a trailer with no title, then a website with no explanation.
f:clueless: Jane Austen’s Emma in a Beverly Hills high school.
f:coachman: The first Korean film to win a major international prize, at Berlin.
f:collateral: Shot Los Angeles at night on digital video so the sky glowed orange.
f:collective: Sports journalists follow a deadly nightclub fire into the hospitals and find a national healthcare fraud.
f:colorpomegranates: A life of an Armenian poet told in living tableaux. Soviet censors recut it; its director was later jailed on trumped-up charges.
f:colorpurple: Nominated for eleven Academy prizes and won none; a talk-show host’s acting debut.
f:comeandsee: A Belarusian boy joins the partisans; live ammunition was fired close over the actors’ heads. Its director never made another film.
f:comedrink: A female swordfighter in a cavernous inn; its director soon left the studio to make his next film in Taiwan.
f:comingamerica: A humorist’s lawsuit over its story exposed how the studio’s accounting kept even a hit "unprofitable."
f:conan24: The 27th film in a series that sells more tickets every spring.
f:conformist: A Fascist agent sent to kill his old professor; its colours and compositions shaped a generation of American directors.
f:constantine: A comic-book exorcist relocated from London to Los Angeles, directed by a music-video director on his first feature; its Gabriel is Tilda Swinton.
f:contagion: Its bat-to-pig-to-chef origin story was watched again by millions in 2020.
f:contempt: A great German director plays himself making a film of the Odyssey.
f:conversation: A surveillance expert who tears his flat apart; released months before Watergate brought down a president.
f:coolhandluke: A decorated veteran on a Southern chain gang who will not be broken, eats fifty eggs on a bet, and gives the warden a line about failures to communicate.
f:copperfield35: A distant ancestor of the 2019 adaptation on your list.
f:corbeau: Poison-pen letters in a provincial town. Made for a German-controlled company, it got its director banned after the Liberation.
f:coyotevsacme: Finished in 2023 and shelved by its own studio for a tax write-off; after a public outcry a small distributor bought and released it.
f:cranesflying: The first Soviet film to win the Riviera’s top prize, with astonishing handheld camerawork.
f:crazyrichasians: The first Hollywood studio film with a majority Asian cast in twenty-five years; shot in Singapore and Malaysia.
f:cremator: A fussy Prague crematorium manager is seduced by Nazism. Finished as Soviet tanks rolled in, it was shelved for twenty years.
f:crieswhispers: A manor house in red, where a sister is dying.
f:crocodiledundee: Australia’s biggest film ever: "That’s not a knife. That’s a knife."
f:cronos: Its director’s debut, made after he worked for years as a makeup effects artist.
f:crossroads: One of the first Japanese films shown widely in Europe.
f:crouchingtiger: The highest-grossing foreign-language film in American history; its bamboo-top duel took two weeks.
f:crow: Its star, the son of a martial-arts legend, was killed on set by a gun loaded with a lodged bullet fragment.
f:crowd: An ordinary man among thousands of identical office desks.
f:crowssparrows: Made in secret during the last months of the civil war.
f:cryinggame: Its distributor built the campaign around asking critics not to reveal its twist.
f:cuckoonest: The second film to win all five main Academy prizes; shot in a real Oregon state hospital.
f:curiousyellow: Seized by US customs as obscene; its court victory changed American censorship.
f:cyclist: An Afghan refugee rides a bicycle in circles for a week to pay for his wife’s hospital bills.
f:cyrano90: In rhyming alexandrines, with English subtitles written in rhyme by Anthony Burgess.
f:dahomey: Twenty-six looted treasures return from Paris to Benin, and one of them narrates.
f:daisies: Two young women decide the world is spoiled and act accordingly; banned for wasting food on screen.
f:dalmatians: Xerography cut the cost of animation and gave it a sketchy new look.
f:dambusters: Britain’s biggest hit of 1955; its bomb run inspired a famous space-battle finale 22 years later.
f:damnation: Rain, dogs and a bar called the Titanik, in endless tracking shots.
f:damnedunited: Brian Clough’s 44 days at Leeds United; its source novel was sued by a real footballer.
f:dancerdark: Its musical numbers were shot with a hundred fixed digital cameras.
f:danceswolves: Called Kevin’s Gate before release; a three-hour western with subtitled Lakota that made over $400 million.
f:dancingdaughters: The flapper film that made its star.
f:dangal: A wrestler trains his daughters to win what he never did; a phenomenon in China, too.
f:dangerousgame: Shot on the same jungle sets, at the same time, as a certain giant ape.
f:darkknight: Its supporting lead died six months before release; his performance won posthumously. Shot partly on IMAX film cameras.
f:dasboot: Shot in a full-size U-boat on a gimballed rig; the cast stayed indoors for months to stay pale.
f:dave: A presidential lookalike takes over when the president has a stroke; real senators and pundits played themselves.
f:dawnofdead: Survivors hole up in a shopping mall; shot at night after the Pennsylvania mall closed.
f:dayearthstill: A visitor from space warns humanity about nuclear war; its robot’s command phrase became a geek password.
f:dayfornight: A film about making a film, with its director playing the director.
f:dayofwrath: A witch trial made in occupied Denmark; its director fled to Sweden soon after.
f:daysbeingwild: A flop with the biggest young cast in Hong Kong, it ends with a character never seen again.
f:daysofheaven: A Texas wheat farm shot in Alberta, mostly in the "magic hour" before sunset. Its director then vanished from filmmaking for twenty years.
f:daysyouth: The earliest surviving film by a director later ranked among the greatest.
f:dazedconfused: The last day of school in 1976 Texas; a local actor’s first line ‘alright, alright, alright’ followed him forever.
f:ddlj: Played continuously at one Bombay cinema, the Maratha Mandir, for over twenty-five years.
f:deadalive: Used about three hundred litres of fake blood per minute in its lawnmower finale.
f:deadman: Neil Young improvised its guitar score live while watching the film.
f:deadofnight: An anthology of tales ending with a malevolent ventriloquist’s dummy.
f:deadpool: Its star lobbied for eleven years; leaked test footage forced the studio’s hand.
f:deadreckoning: Its star rode a motorbike off a Norwegian cliff six times; the film opened a week before the Barbenheimer weekend and lost its big screens to it.
f:deathbyhanging: A Korean man survives his execution, and the officials must re-enact his crime to make him understand it.
f:deathfuneral: A family funeral undone by hallucinogens, a naked uncle and a blackmailer; its director once performed Yoda and Miss Piggy. Remade in America three years later with one actor repeating his role.
f:decisiontoleave: A detective falls for the widow he suspects; the whole romance is conducted through translation apps.
f:declineempire: Montreal history professors talk about sex while cooking dinner.
f:deerhunter: Pennsylvania steelworkers go to Vietnam; its Russian-roulette scenes had no historical basis.
f:deewaar: Two brothers, a gangster and a cop. "Mere paas maa hai" ("I have mother") is probably the most quoted line in Hindi film.
f:deliverance: Four suburban men canoe a Georgia river before it is dammed; its banjo duet became a hit record.
f:demonpond: A kabuki star of female roles plays both a village bride and the dragon princess of the pond; ends in a flood of miniature models.
f:demonslayer1: Overtook Spirited Away as Japan’s highest-grossing film ever.
f:departed: A remake of a Hong Kong film that finally won its director his Oscar; presented by three old friends.
f:dersuuzala: A Japanese master’s comeback, made in the Siberian taiga for the Soviets.
f:despicable: Animated in Paris; its gibberish-speaking henchmen became the most profitable characters of the decade.
f:destiny: A young woman bargains with Death across three eras; it inspired at least one great director to take up film.
f:destiny97: A lifetime achievement prize at the Côte came the same year.
f:detour: Made in days on a tiny budget at a poverty-row studio; now a cult noir landmark.
f:devdas02: The most expensive Indian film yet; one heroine’s costumes weighed thirty kilos.
f:devdas35: The first of many screen versions of the tragic lover, made in Bengali and Hindi.
f:diaboliques: Its end credits begged audiences not to spoil the twist.
f:diamondarm: A timid economist returns from a cruise with smuggled jewels in his plaster cast; seen by more than 76 million Soviets.
f:diamondsforever: Its original star came back for one more, for a then-record fee he gave to charity.
f:dickjohnsondead: A cinematographer stages increasingly elaborate deaths for her father as his dementia advances, so they can rehearse the real one.
f:dicktracy: A comic strip filmed in only seven colours.
f:diehard: Its lead, a TV comic, was paid a then-shocking $5 million; its British villain’s first film role. "Yippee-ki-yay."
f:dil90: The biggest Hindi hit of its year.
f:dilchahta: A first film that made Bombay youth films modern overnight.
f:dilse: Its opening song was danced on top of a moving train.
f:dingjun: China’s first film, a recording of Peking opera made at a Beijing photo studio; now lost.
f:disclosureday: Its director returned to alien contact nearly fifty years after his first film about it.
f:discreetcharm: Six friends try, and fail, to finish a dinner.
f:distantvoices: A Liverpool family in the 1940s and ’50s remembered through pub singalongs.
f:district9: Shot in a real Soweto slum being cleared for relocation.
f:diva: A postman bootlegs an opera singer who refuses to record; it launched the glossy "cinéma du look."
f:divingbell: A magazine editor, paralysed but for one eyelid, dictates a memoir blink by blink; much of it seen through his one eye.
f:divorcee: A frank pre-censorship drama in which a wife answers infidelity with her own.
f:django: A drifter dragging a coffin; so violent it was banned in Britain for decades, and dozens of unofficial sequels borrowed its name.
f:dobigha: A farmer pulls a rickshaw in Calcutta to save his land; Indian neorealism, honoured at the Riviera.
f:dodeskaden: Its director’s first colour film; its failure left him unable to find Japanese backing for years.
f:dogday: A real 1972 Brooklyn bank robbery staged to pay for a lover’s surgery. "Attica! Attica!"
f:dogslife: The first film under a million-dollar deal.
f:dogville: A whole town drawn in chalk on a black sound-stage floor.
f:dolcevita: A wade in the Trevi Fountain and a photographer called Paparazzo, who gave the world a word.
f:dolemite: A stand-up comic’s rhyming pimp persona, funded by his party records; the boom mic dips into shot again and again.
f:donabarbara: Made its lead the most famous woman in Mexican film.
f:donaflor: A widow’s dead first husband returns, naked, to share her bed; Brazil’s box-office record for 34 years.
f:doncamillo: A priest and a communist mayor feud in a village; a huge hit in France and Italy with four sequels.
f:dongju: The first film by a novelist who would become Korea’s culture minister.
f:donjuan: The first feature with a synchronised recorded score and sound effects.
f:donniedarko: A jet engine falls on a house weeks after 9/11; bombed, then ran at midnight in London for years.
f:dontlookback: A folk singer’s British tour, opening with him flipping cue cards to his own song.
f:dontlooknow: Venice in winter and a small figure in a red coat; its love scene is cut against the couple dressing afterwards.
f:dotherightthing: One block of Bed-Stuy on the hottest day of the year; "Fight the Power" playing from a boombox.
f:doubleindemnity: An insurance salesman and a murderous wife: a blueprint for film noir.
f:doublelife: Two identical women in Kraków and Paris; seventeen prints were each cut slightly differently.
f:downfall: Its bunker-rant scene became the internet’s most-subtitled clip.
f:dracula31: A Spanish-language version was shot on the same sets at night.
f:dracula92: Its director fired the effects team and made every effect in-camera, the old way.
f:dragoninn: Swordfighters gather at a desert inn to protect a family from eunuch assassins. A record-breaking hit across Asia that set the style of the modern wuxia film.
f:dreams25: The last of a trilogy about sex, love and dreams made in Oslo.
f:dreams90: Eight of its director’s own dreams, one with an actor playing Van Gogh; financed with American help.
f:drive11: A scorpion jacket, a toothpick, and a synth-pop soundtrack; the most imitated look of the decade.
f:drivemycar: Three hours: a theatre director grieving his wife rehearses a multilingual Uncle Vanya in Hiroshima while a young woman drives his red Saab.
f:drivingmissdaisy: Won the top prize without its director even being nominated; its lead, at 80, was then the oldest winner of her category.
f:drno: The first film of the longest-running spy series, made for about a million dollars.
f:drunkenangel: The first pairing of a director and the star who would appear in sixteen of his films.
f:drunkenmaster: Made its young star’s comic kung fu a sensation.
f:drunkenmaster2: Its lead fired the director over style and finished the final fight himself; he walked on hot coals for real.
f:dubarry: Released in America as a new title, it made its director and star international names.
f:ducksoup: A disappointment on release; now its stars’ most celebrated film.
f:duellists: An advertising director’s first feature, lit like Georgian paintings.
f:duelsun: Nicknamed “Lust in the Dust”; the top film of its year thanks to a saturation release.
f:dumbo: Made cheaply and quickly to recover the studio’s losses; it did.
f:dune2: The Harkonnen home world was shot in infrared, so the black sun turns skin chalk-white.
f:dustin: A short film: a trans woman in a crowd of ravers in an abandoned warehouse, as the night winds down.
f:earth: A lyrical film about collective farming that the authorities attacked as insufficiently political.
f:earthquake: Shown in "Sensurround," whose rumbling speakers cracked plaster in some cinemas.
f:easternpromises: A Russian mob driver in London, told through his tattoos; its star fought naked in a bathhouse on tiled floors.
f:easyrider: Made for about $400,000; its takings sent studios hunting for anyone under thirty with a script.
f:edwardscissor: An unfinished man with scissors for hands in pastel suburbia; the last screen role of a horror legend.
f:eeaao: A laundromat owner doing her taxes learns to jump between universes. A $25 million film with hot-dog fingers won seven Oscars, and a former child actor returned after decades away to win one.
f:eega12: A murdered man returns as a housefly to take revenge.
f:eggandi: Two supporting characters got a long-running series of their own.
f:eightandahalf: A famous director with nothing left to say makes a film about having nothing to say. Titled for the number of films its maker had made.
f:eighthundred: The top-grossing film in the world in 2020, released while Western cinemas stayed shut.
f:eightmile: Its rapper star skipped the Oscars; the song won anyway.
f:elcid: A Hollywood epic built in Spain with thousands of extras.
f:eldiaquemequieras: Shot in New York for Latin American audiences; its singer-star died in a plane crash months later.
f:election05: A triad votes for its chairman every two years; the loser won’t accept it. Mainland China refused to release it.
f:election2: Also called Triad Election; a triad chairman who wants to go legitimate finds Beijing prefers him in charge.
f:election99: A civics teacher sabotages an overachiever’s student-council campaign; a flop in cinemas that became a cult on video.
f:elemental: Opened to the weakest start in its studio’s history, then kept playing for months.
f:elephantman: Its producer, a famous comic, kept his name off it so audiences wouldn’t expect a comedy.
f:elevatortothegallo58: Its trumpet score was improvised in one night, watching the film.
f:elippathayam: A Kerala landlord trapped in his crumbling ancestral house as feudalism dies.
f:eliteSquad: A pirated copy was seen by millions in Brazil before release.
f:elmstreet: Saved its tiny distributor, nicknamed "the house that Freddy built." A young actor’s first role.
f:eltopo: The first "midnight movie": it ran for months at a New York cinema after a Beatle championed it.
f:emigrants: Swedish farmers sail to Minnesota in the 1840s; its director also shot and edited it.
f:emiliaperez: A cartel boss’s gender transition as a Spanish-language musical, shot in France. It led the Oscar nominations, then its campaign collapsed after its star’s old posts surfaced.
f:empirestrikes: Its producer financed it himself with the first film’s profits; the twist was kept even from most of the cast.
f:endgame: The highest-grossing film of all time for a while; its three-hour run had theatres open around the clock.
f:endoftour: Five days on the road between a Rolling Stone reporter and a novelist at the end of his book tour.
f:englishpatient: Fox dropped it weeks before shooting; its editor cut it on a digital system, the first to win the editing Oscar that way.
f:englishvinglish12: Its star's return after fifteen years away.
f:enterdragon: The first Hollywood-Hong Kong co-production. Its star died six days before its premiere.
f:entertainer: A fading music-hall comic in a dying seaside town, played by Britain’s greatest actor in the role that reinvented him.
f:enthiran: The most expensive Indian film of its day; its star plays both a scientist and his android.
f:enthusiasmsymphony30: The first Soviet sound documentary, recorded on location in the mines with machines built for the job.
f:entracte: A Dada film made to fill the interval of a ballet, with two famous artists playing chess on a rooftop.
f:eo: A grey circus donkey wanders across Poland and Italy; six donkeys played him. Its director was 84.
f:eraserhead: Shot over five years at night in old stables at the American Film Institute; its director delivered newspapers to pay for it.
f:erastour: The singer bypassed the studios and booked the film directly with the biggest cinema chain; the highest-grossing concert film ever.
f:escapenewyork: Manhattan as a maximum-security prison in 1997; much of it shot in fire-gutted East St. Louis.
f:et: Overtook the space opera as the biggest film of all time; a sweets company that let its brand be used saw sales triple.
f:europaeuropa: A Jewish boy survives by passing as a Hitler Youth member; Germany refused to submit it for the foreign-language Oscar.
f:evildead: Shot in a Tennessee cabin by Michigan students; a famous novelist’s rave at Cannes sold it.
f:exhuma: Shamans and a geomancer dig up a cursed grave; one of the biggest Korean horror hits ever.
f:exile31: The first sound feature produced by an African American company.
f:exiled: Macau just before the handover; gunmen sent to kill an old friend end up helping him. A spiritual sequel to The Mission with much of the same cast.
f:exorcist: Audiences fainted in the aisles. The first horror film nominated for Best Picture.
f:exterminating: Guests at a dinner party find they cannot leave the room, for no reason anyone can name. Made in Mexico on a tight budget.
f:eyeswide: Shot for 400 days, the longest continuous shoot on record; its director died four days after delivering it.
f:f1movie: Shot during real Grand Prix weekends, with its star driving a modified car on track between sessions; the streamer’s biggest cinema hit.
f:fabelmans: The director’s own boyhood, ending with a teenage meeting with an old master of westerns.
f:faces68: Shot over six months in his own house, cut over three years.
f:fahrenheit911: The highest-grossing documentary ever released; dropped by its original distributor’s parent.
f:fallingleaves12: Made at her own studio across the river, where a sign told the actors to Be Natural.
f:fallout: Its star broke his ankle jumping between rooftops, and the take is in the film.
f:fannyalexander: A five-hour TV version and a three-hour cinema cut; announced as its director’s farewell to film.
f:fantasia: Required its own sound system in cinemas. Lost money at first; found its audience in later decades.
f:fantasmagorie: Often called the first fully hand-drawn animated cartoon: about 700 drawings in under two minutes.
f:fantomas: A serial about a master criminal who always escapes; the surrealists adored it.
f:farewellconcubine: Fifty years of two Peking opera actors; banned twice at home, then released cut.
f:fargo: Claims to be a true story; it isn’t. They had to truck in snow because Minnesota had a warm winter.
f:fassbinderswomen: A television documentary in which the actresses of Rainer Werner Fassbinder’s troupe talk about working and living with him.
f:fastfive: Turned a street-racing series into a globe-trotting heist franchise, dragging a bank vault through Rio.
f:fatalattraction: Test audiences demanded the killer die; a new ending was shot.
f:favourite: Queen Anne’s court shot with fisheye lenses and candlelight; seventeen rabbits in the royal bedroom.
f:feeauxchoux: A fairy plucks babies from cabbages; among the very first narrative fiction films.
f:fellowship: All three films were shot at once over 274 days; its studio bet the company on it after another studio wanted it cut to one film.
f:festen: The first Dogme 95 film, shot on a consumer camcorder under a vow of chastity.
f:fewgoodmen: Its writer wrote the play on cocktail napkins while tending bar on Broadway.
f:fforfake: An essay on an art forger, his hoaxing biographer and, slyly, its own director.
f:fiddler: Shot in Yugoslavia; its cinematographer used a stocking over the lens for an earthy look.
f:fifthelement: Written by its director at sixteen; the most expensive European film at the time.
f:fightclub: A flop whose studio chief was fired, it became a DVD phenomenon; its first rule became a meme.
f:finalreckoning: Its star hung from a biplane’s wing at eight thousand feet; one of the most expensive films ever made.
f:fire96: Cinemas showing it in India were attacked by mobs.
f:fireman: A rescue shown from inside and outside the burning house: an early step toward film editing.
f:firemensball: Banned “forever” after the 1968 invasion; its director left for America.
f:firstreformed: Its seventy-one-year-old writer-director finally made his version of the transcendental style he had written about in 1972.
f:fishermen: The first Chinese film to win a prize abroad, at Moscow in 1935.
f:fishwanda: Its 78-year-old director, an old studio comedy veteran, came back after twenty years away.
f:fistful: A cheap Italian-Spanish-German western, uncredited remake of a samurai film, whose makers were sued by its original director. It started a genre.
f:fistfury: Its hero smashes a "No dogs and Chinese allowed" sign in Shanghai.
f:fitzcarraldo: A 320-ton steamship hauled over a Peruvian mountain, for real, with no special effects.
f:fiveeasypieces: A diner scene about a chicken-salad sandwich became a counterculture anthem.
f:fjord: Its director’s second Palme, nineteen years after his first.
f:flee: An animated documentary, so its Afghan refugee subject could stay anonymous.
f:fleshdevil: Its stars’ romance continued off screen, to the delight of the press.
f:floatingweeds: A travelling actor visits his secret son; its director’s colour remake of his own 1934 silent film, shot at another studio.
f:flow24: A cat survives a flood in a wordless animated film made in free open-source software; Latvia’s first Oscar.
f:flowerstrees: The first cartoon in full three-colour Technicolor, and winner of the first animated-short prize.
f:flyingdowntorio33: Fifth-billed, a dancing couple stole it and were made a team.
f:fnaf: Opened simultaneously on streaming and still made ten times its budget, carried by fans of the video game.
f:fogofwar: Robert McNamara speaks into its director’s Interrotron, a teleprompter rig that lets subjects look him in the eye through the lens.
f:foolishwives: Promoted as the first million-dollar picture, which its director’s excesses made true.
f:forbiddenplanet: Shakespeare’s Tempest in space, with an all-electronic score.
f:forrestgump: Digitally inserted its hero into newsreels with three presidents; the studio claimed it had never turned a profit.
f:fortythousand: The charge at Beersheba, a hit at home and abroad.
f:fourweddings: Made for under £3 million, it became the highest-grossing British film to that date.
f:frank10: The first screen Frankenstein, thought lost until a collector’s print surfaced in the 1970s.
f:frank31: Its flat-headed monster make-up became so iconic the studio trademarked it.
f:frankenstein25: The project its director had wanted to make since childhood.
f:freaks: Cast real sideshow performers. Banned in Britain for thirty years, it nearly ended its director’s career.
f:freefire: An arms deal in a Boston warehouse in 1978 goes wrong for ninety minutes straight.
f:freesolo: A climber scales El Capitan without a rope; the crew worried they would film him die.
f:frenchconnection: Its car-versus-train chase was shot on real Brooklyn streets, largely without permits.
f:frenzy: Its director’s return to London, set in the Covent Garden market where his father had traded.
f:freshman: A college boy desperate to be popular; its football finale was the template for decades of campus comedies.
f:fromhere: A kiss on the beach in the surf; a singer’s comeback in a supporting role.
f:frostnixon: A British TV host buys an interview with the disgraced president and gets the apology; both leads came straight from the stage production.
f:frozen: Its villain became its heroine late in development once the song let it go.
f:fugitive: Its bus-and-train crash used a real train, and the wreckage was left at the location as a tourist attraction.
f:fullmetaljacket: Vietnam recreated in a derelict London gasworks, with palm trees imported from Spain; its drill instructor was a real one.
f:fullmonty: Made for $3.5 million; out-grossed everything in Britain except Titanic.
f:fullriverred: A Song dynasty murder mystery told in near real time, and its director’s biggest hit.
f:funeralroses: Oedipus among Tokyo’s gay-bar underground; a stated influence on a certain clockwork British film.
f:funnyfaces: Chalk drawings come alive, one of the first animated films.
f:funnygames97: Its killers talk to the camera and rewind the film when things go wrong for them.
f:funnygirl: Its lead tied for the acting prize with Katharine Hepburn, the only exact tie ever in that category.
f:furious7: Its co-star died midway through the shoot; his brothers stood in and the ending became a farewell.
f:fury36: The exiled director’s first American film, about a lynch mob.
f:gandhi: Twenty years in the making; the funeral scene used some 300,000 extras, a record.
f:gangsny: Lower Manhattan in 1863 rebuilt at Cinecittà.
f:gangsofwasseypur: A five-hour coal-mafia saga across three generations, cut in two.
f:gaslight44: Its plot gave the language a word for making someone doubt their own mind.
f:gatehell: Its dazzling colour photography won in Cannes and Hollywood.
f:gatesofheaven: Two California pet cemeteries and their owners. A German director ate his own shoe on film after betting its maker would finish it.
f:gendarme: Made its lead France’s biggest star at fifty; five sequels followed.
f:general: A real steam engine plunged through a burning bridge, one of the costliest single shots of the silent era. It flopped; its reputation came later.
f:gentlemans: A reporter pretends to be Jewish to expose antisemitism.
f:gertie: The first cartoon character with a personality. Its creator performed live on stage beside her.
f:gertrud: Its director’s last film, booed in Paris and later hailed as a summation.
f:getaway72: Its two stars fell in love on set and married.
f:getcarter: A London gangster goes home to Newcastle for his brother’s funeral, and revenge.
f:getout: A sketch comedian’s first film; made for four and a half million, it grossed over two hundred and fifty.
f:ghajini: The first Hindi film to gross ₹100 crore in India.
f:ghazalbanat: Its comic star died before filming ended; the film is still one of the most loved in the Arab world.
f:ghost: A murdered banker haunts his girlfriend; its pottery-wheel scene was parodied for thirty years.
f:ghostbusters: Written for two comics, one of whom died before shooting.
f:ghostprotocol: Its star climbed the outside of the world’s tallest building himself.
f:ghostshell: Its opening became a reference point for a Wachowski film four years later.
f:giant: Its youngest star died before it was finished.
f:giftshop: Directed by an anonymous street artist; nobody is sure how much of it is a prank.
f:gilda: A single glove removed became one of the most famous scenes in Hollywood.
f:gimmeshelter: A free concert at Altamont where a man is killed in front of the cameras.
f:gladiator: Started with thirty pages of script; its actor playing Proximo died mid-shoot and was finished digitally.
f:glassonion: Played a single week in cinemas before streaming; the streamer paid a reported $400 million for two sequels.
f:glengarry: Its most famous scene, a motivational speech from hell, was written for the film.
f:gobetween: "The past is a foreign country: they do things differently there."
f:godcreated: Made its star an international phenomenon and earned more in America than any French film before it.
f:goddess: A mother who sells herself to pay for her son’s schooling; a peak of Chinese silent film.
f:godfather: The studio nearly fired its director several times. Its lead declined his Academy prize, sending an Apache activist to explain why.
f:godfather2: The first sequel to win the top Academy prize; two actors won for playing the same man.
f:godfather3: Made to pay off its director’s debts; his daughter replaced an actress who dropped out the day before shooting.
f:godfrey: A socialite finds a “forgotten man” at a city dump during a scavenger hunt and hires him as her butler. Nominated in all four acting categories, a first.
f:godscountry: Canada’s most successful silent film, notorious for its star’s nude swim.
f:godzilla: A monster born of nuclear testing, nine years after Hiroshima; the start of a franchise still running.
f:godzillaminusone: The first film in its series to win an Oscar, for effects made by a team of about 35 people on a budget smaller than one Hollywood action scene. Its director supervised the effects himself.
f:golddiggers29: An all-colour musical, now mostly lost.
f:golddiggers33: Ends with a lament for forgotten war veterans in the Depression.
f:goldfinger: A woman painted gold, a laser, a gadget-filled car: the formula locked in.
f:goldrush: A starving prospector eats his boot, and two bread rolls do a dance.
f:gomorrah: Its source’s author lives under police protection.
f:gonewind: The biggest hit of the era by far, adjusted for inflation still near the top. Its romanticised slave South was criticised then and now.
f:goodbadugly: Three men and a buried fortune across the American Civil War, shot in Spain; its three-way standoff and score are endlessly copied.
f:goodbyechips: Its lead beat a famous rival from the biggest film of the year to the acting prize.
f:goodbyeporkpie: A road movie in a yellow Mini the length of New Zealand; the first big local hit.
f:goodearth: A story of Chinese farmers with white stars in the leads; the studio passed over a Chinese American star for the heroine.
f:goodfellas: A real gangster’s life in voice-over; one unbroken Steadicam shot through the Copacabana kitchen made it famous.
f:goodwillhunting: Two childhood friends from Boston wrote it as a thriller and sold it to have leading roles.
f:gosfordpark: Its writer later created a similar country-house TV drama.
f:gospel: An atheist Marxist’s life of Christ, cast with peasants and his own mother, dedicated to a pope and praised by the Vatican newspaper.
f:gosta: The breakthrough of an 18-year-old actress whose director took her to Hollywood.
f:graduate: An aimless graduate and an older woman; its unknown lead was far from a typical leading man.
f:grandeillusion: Banned by the Nazis; its original negative was seized and later found in Moscow.
f:grandevadrouille: Two Frenchmen help British airmen escape occupied France; France’s biggest film for over thirty years.
f:grandhotel: Packed with stars; its most famous line is a wish to be left alone.
f:gravefireflies: Two orphans in the firebombing of Kobe; released on the same bill as a cheerful forest spirit.
f:gravity: Its star spent weeks alone in a light box with the camera on a robot arm.
f:greatbeauty: A sixty-five-year-old writer drifts through Rome’s terrace parties looking for the beauty he glimpsed at eighteen.
f:greatdictator: A satire of Hitler begun before the war; its director later said he could not have made it had he known the full horror.
f:greatescape: Its lead did most of his own motorcycle riding, and played a pursuing German soldier in some shots.
f:greatestshow: The top film of 1952 and a surprise top-prize winner over a classic western.
f:greatsilence: A mute gunfighter in snowbound Utah, and the villains win. A happy ending was shot for markets that objected.
f:greed: The director’s cut ran around eight hours; the studio cut it to about two and a quarter, and the rest is film history’s most famous lost footage.
f:greenknight: An Arthurian quest filmed in Ireland; the fox talks.
f:greenray: Largely improvised by its lead; premiered on television before cinemas.
f:greenvalley: Beat the most famous film of its year for the top prize.
f:gremlins: Don’t get them wet, keep them out of light, never feed them after midnight.
f:groundhog: Its star and director stopped speaking during the shoot and did not reconcile for twenty years.
f:guardians: A talking raccoon and a tree who says three words, sold on a mixtape of seventies hits.
f:guerragaucha: One of the biggest hits in Argentine film history.
f:guesswho: Its lead actor died weeks after filming ended; his co-star never watched it.
f:guise: Made to give cinema theatrical respectability; its score was written by a leading French composer.
f:gulliver39: A rival studio’s answer to the first cel-animated feature.
f:guncrazy: A doomed outlaw couple; co-written under a front’s name by a blacklisted writer.
f:gungajumna: Two brothers on opposite sides of the law: the template for decades of Bombay action films.
f:hababam: Unruly boarding-school pupils versus their teachers; Turks still quote it by heart.
f:hahk: A three-hour family wedding musical with fourteen songs; for years the biggest hit in Indian history. Cinemas refurbished their screens for it.
f:hailmary: A schoolteacher wakes alone on a spaceship with no memory, and his only friend is an alien who talks in musical chords, played by a puppeteer on set.
f:hallelujah: One of the first major-studio films with an all-Black cast.
f:halloween: Its killer’s mask was a cheap mask of a starship captain, painted white.
f:hamilton20: Filmed at three live performances in 2016 and released onto a streamer four years later.
f:hamlet21: Its star played the prince as a woman raised as a boy.
f:hamlet48: The first non-American film to win the top Academy prize.
f:hamnet: Shakespeare’s wife grieves the death of their son, whose name he later gives to a play. The final scene at the Globe left festival audiences in tears.
f:hanabi: Its director painted the paintings in the film while recovering from a motorbike crash that half-paralysed his face.
f:handofgod: Its director’s Naples adolescence, the summer Maradona arrived and his parents died.
f:happenednight: A small studio’s modest comedy that swept the five biggest prizes. Undershirt sales reportedly slumped after its star took off his shirt to reveal none.
f:happiness98: Its studio’s parent refused to release it.
f:happytogether: Shot in Buenos Aires with no script; its director’s last film before the handover.
f:harakiri: A masterless samurai asks to commit ritual suicide at a lord’s house and slowly reveals why. A demolition of the samurai code it seems to honour.
f:hardboiled: Ends with a hospital shootout including a two-minute-forty-second single take through two floors.
f:hardday: A day in the life of the most famous band in the world; its style shaped the music video.
f:haridas: Ran for three years at one Madras cinema.
f:harishchandra: India’s first full-length feature. No actresses would take part, so men played the women’s roles.
f:harlancounty: A year inside a Kentucky coal strike; its crew were shot at on the picket line.
f:haroldmaude: A death-obsessed youth loves a 79-year-old free spirit. A flop that played for years at one Minneapolis cinema.
f:harrysally: "I’ll have what she’s having," said by its director’s mother.
f:hatefuleight: Shot on 70mm Ultra Panavision lenses last used on a 1966 film; Morricone’s first western score in forty years.
f:hausu: Seven schoolgirls, a hungry house, a piano that eats fingers; its director took story ideas from his young daughter.
f:havenot: Its 19-year-old lead met her future husband on set; a famous line about whistling came from here.
f:havocheaven: The Monkey King against the heavenly court; made in two parts over four years.
f:haxan: Half lecture, half nightmare; censored for decades, then relaunched in 1968 with a Beat-writer narration.
f:heartofglass76: Most of its cast acted under hypnosis.
f:heat: The first scene its two stars ever shared on screen; the downtown shootout audio was recorded live.
f:heathers: Grossed about a million dollars in cinemas; its high-school body count and slang made it a video-shop cult. "What’s your damage?"
f:heatofnight: A Black Philadelphia detective and a Mississippi sheriff; one slap back became famous.
f:heavenlycreatures: Two Christchurch schoolgirls kill one girl’s mother; the first work of a digital effects shop that would soon be famous.
f:heavensgate: Its cost overruns sank United Artists, which was sold within months; the end of the director-led New Hollywood.
f:hedwig: An East German rock singer’s story, from a show that started in a drag club; its songs by a composer who played in the band.
f:hellhighwater: Two brothers rob branches of the bank foreclosing on their mother’s West Texas ranch.
f:hellodolly: A hit on paper that lost money; its cost helped push its studio to the brink.
f:hellsangels: Three years in the making; the producer reshot it for sound and several pilots died filming the dogfights.
f:henryv: Shakespeare as wartime morale-booster, shot in Ireland with extras from the local defence force.
f:henryviii: The first British film to win an American acting prize, and a hit that made Britain’s industry believe in itself.
f:her13: Shanghai stood in for a near-future Los Angeles; the operating system’s voice was recast after filming ended.
f:hercules58: A cheap Italian sword-and-sandal film that a savvy distributor turned into a US hit, launching a craze.
f:here23: A Romanian builder in Brussels clears out his fridge before a trip home and meets a Chinese-Belgian botanist who studies moss. Eighty minutes, shot on 16mm.
f:hero02: Its American distributor shelved it for two years; when finally released it opened at number one. Each version of the story has its own colour.
f:hiddenfortress: Two bickering peasants tell the story; a young American director later borrowed the idea for a space fantasy.
f:highhopes: A couple of King’s Cross socialists, a cactus, and a visit to Marx’s grave; its director develops scripts through months of improvisation.
f:highnoon: A marshal abandoned by his town, in real time; its writer was blacklisted during production.
f:highsociety: A musical remake of the 1940 film on your list; its female lead’s last role before royalty.
f:himala: A village girl claims to see the Virgin Mary, and a pilgrimage industry follows.
f:himom: A comedian’s tribute to her late mother; its first-time director became the highest-grossing solo female director in the world.
f:hindrajab: Rebuilt around the real recorded phone call of a six-year-old trapped in a car in Gaza.
f:hiroshima: A French actress and a Japanese architect in Hiroshima, fourteen years after the bomb. Withdrawn from the Riviera competition to avoid upsetting the Americans.
f:historyboys: Eight Sheffield grammar-school boys cramming for Oxford and Cambridge, filmed with the original stage cast straight off the National Theatre tour.
f:holdovers: Made to look and sound like a film from 1970, when it is set.
f:holidayinn: Introduced a Christmas song that became the best-selling single of all time.
f:holygrail: Coconut halves instead of horses; partly funded by rock bands including Pink Floyd and Led Zeppelin.
f:holyspider: A journalist hunts a serial killer in Mashhad; shot in Jordan because it could never be made in Iran.
f:homealone: A family forgets their son on a trip to Paris; the biggest live-action comedy in history for years, made by a writer-producer who had fled Chicago for Hollywood and then back.
f:homealone2: Features a cameo by a real estate developer who owned the Plaza Hotel and made it a condition of shooting there.
f:hoopdreams: Planned as a thirty-minute short; five years and 250 hours of footage later, the Academy’s failure to nominate it forced a rule change.
f:hope19: Drawn from its director’s own life: a woman in Oslo is told over Christmas that her cancer has spread to her brain, and her long partnership has to become a marriage.
f:hoppers: A girl transfers her mind into a robot beaver to talk to animals.
f:horrordracula: Blood in colour: the start of a small British studio’s horror empire.
f:horsemen: The year’s biggest hit; one tango scene made an unknown into a phenomenon.
f:horusprinceofthesu68: Its young animators included the future founders of the house of the bus-shaped cat.
f:hospitality: A family feud comedy with a waterfall rescue its star performed himself.
f:host06: Its river creature was inspired by a real case of formaldehyde dumped into the Han River by a US military morgue.
f:housemaid: A domestic thriller of lust and rat poison, remade in 2010 and cited by later Korean masters.
f:houseofusher: First of a cycle of eight Poe adaptations; the drive-in studio’s first film in colour and widescreen, shot in fifteen days.
f:houseofwax: A major-studio 3D hit directed by a man who could not see in 3D.
f:howthewest: Shot in three-camera Cinerama, one of only two narrative films made in the format.
f:hpstone: Its author insisted on an all-British cast; its young leads grew up on screen across a decade.
f:hunger: Its central conversation between a hunger striker and a priest runs seventeen minutes in one static shot.
f:hunterwali: A masked heroine with a whip; the surprise smash that made its star a sensation.
f:hurtlocker: The lowest-grossing Best Picture winner in modern times; the first woman to win Best Director beat her ex-husband’s blockbuster.
f:hwrevue: Introduced a rain-soaked song that became the title of a famous musical 23 years later.
f:iamcuba: Ignored in both countries on release; rediscovered in 1992 with the help of two famous American directors.
f:iamnotmadamebovary16: Shot inside a circle frame for most of its length.
f:ifdotdot: Public-school rebels end with machine guns on the chapel roof; it switches between colour and black-and-white, partly to save money.
f:ikarie: A starship crew heads for Alpha Centauri in the 22nd century. Its sets and ideas are often said to have influenced a famous 1968 space odyssey; cut and dubbed as a cheap monster movie for its US release.
f:ikiru: A dying bureaucrat builds a playground.
f:imitation59: Its director’s last and biggest hit, remaking a 1934 film.
f:immigrant: Made under a contract that made its star one of the best-paid people in the world.
f:imstillhere: A mother holds her family together after the dictatorship takes her husband in 1971; the star’s own mother plays her in old age. Brazil’s first Oscar.
f:incendies: Twins read their mother’s will and travel to the Middle East to find the father and brother they never knew.
f:inception: A hallway fight was shot in a rotating corridor built inside an airship hangar in Cardington.
f:inconvenient: A former vice-president’s slide show about climate change.
f:independenceday: Its trailer blew up the White House during the Super Bowl.
f:infernal: Revived Hong Kong film after years of decline; remade as a Best Picture winner in Boston.
f:inferno: Dante’s hell on film: Italy’s first feature and an international hit.
f:infinitycastle: The first part of a trilogy, and the biggest Japanese film ever abroad.
f:ingeborgholm13: Its depiction of the poorhouse prompted a change in Swedish welfare law.
f:inglourious: Its unknown Austrian supporting actor spoke four languages on screen and won everything.
f:inherentvice: A stoned private eye in 1970 Los Angeles; the only film ever adapted from a Pynchon novel.
f:insiang: The first Filipino film shown at Cannes.
f:insideout2: Anxiety moves into a teenager’s head; for a time the highest-grossing animated film ever.
f:intermezzo: Its lead was brought to Hollywood to star in the remake.
f:interstellar: Its black hole was rendered from real physics equations and produced a published scientific paper.
f:inthemoodforlove: Shot over fifteen months with no script; its star wore more than twenty cheongsams.
f:intolerance: Four stories across 2,500 years, cut together; its giant Babylon set stood in Hollywood for years. A costly flop.
f:intothewild: Its director waited ten years for the family of Chris McCandless to agree; the bus scenes were filmed near the real one.
f:intouchables: Seen by nearly twenty million French cinemagoers, a record for a French film at the time.
f:invention: Live action styled like old engravings from a Jules Verne novel.
f:ipcress: A working-class spy in glasses who cooks his own dinner, made by one of the gadget series’ producers as its opposite.
f:irishman: Its stars were de-aged digitally across fifty years; the streamer paid when no studio would.
f:irmavep: A Hong Kong star plays herself cast in a remake of a 1915 serial.
f:irongiant: A marketing flop that its director’s next studio hired him for.
f:ironhorse: The first epic by a director who would define the Western.
f:ironlung: A YouTuber’s adaptation of an indie video game, released through his own company.
f:ironman: Its studio mortgaged its characters to fund it; its lead was considered a bet no other studio would take. Improvised a lot of its dialogue.
f:ironyfate: A drunk Muscovite wakes in an identical flat in Leningrad; broadcast every New Year’s Eve for decades.
f:it: Gave its star her nickname and the language a word for sex appeal.
f:itendswithus: Its production turned into a lawsuit between its two stars.
f:ivan1: Won a state prize; its second part was banned for more than a decade.
f:ivanschildhood: A debut feature that won the Lagoon’s top prize.
f:ivantheterriblepar58: Finished in 1946 and banned by Stalin; released five years after his death.
f:ivanvasilievich: A time machine swaps a Moscow building manager with Ivan the Terrible.
f:jaanebhido: Two photographers stumble on municipal corruption; ends with a Mahabharata staged by the drunk.
f:jaccuse: Its climax shows the war dead rising, played by soldiers on leave.
f:jagteraho56: Directed with Sombhu Mitra; it won the top prize at Karlovy Vary.
f:jaguar79: The first Filipino film in competition at the Côte.
f:jasonargo: Its skeleton sword fight took more than four months to animate.
f:jaws: The mechanical shark barely worked, so its young director kept it out of sight. Opened wide with national TV ads: the first summer blockbuster.
f:jaws2: "Just when you thought it was safe to go back in the water."
f:jazzsinger: The first feature with synchronised spoken dialogue, which ended the silent era. Its star performs in blackface.
f:jeandeflorette: Two Provençal peasants block a spring to ruin the hunchbacked city man who inherits the farm.
f:jeannedielman: Three days of a widow’s routine, nearly in real time. In 2022 critics voted it the greatest film ever made.
f:jedda: Australia’s first colour feature and the first with Aboriginal actors in lead roles.
f:jeevannaiya36: Its leading man walked out mid-shoot and the laboratory assistant took his place, and became a star.
f:jekyll31: The transformation used coloured make-up and matching camera filters, invisible to the audience until it appeared.
f:jfk: Its assassination theories led Congress to pass a law releasing the records.
f:joanarc: Almost all close-ups. The original was thought lost in fires until a complete print turned up in a Norwegian hospital cupboard in 1981.
f:johnnybelinda: Its lead won a top prize for a role without a spoken line.
f:johnnyguitar: A delirious western ignored at home and worshipped by French critics.
