f:johnwick: A stuntman’s directing debut; the dog set everything off.
f:johnwick4: Nearly three hours, climaxing in a fight up 222 steps to Sacré-Cœur.
f:jourdefete: A village postman tries American efficiency; shot in colour and black and white, the colour version was not seen until 1995.
f:journeyitaly: A failing marriage in Naples; the French New Wave called it the first modern film.
f:jsa: The biggest film in Korean history on release; the DMZ set was built in a field.
f:judithofbethulia14: His first feature, made against the wishes of his studio, which fired him for it.
f:junglebook: The last film its studio’s founder oversaw; he died during production.
f:juno: Its writer, a former stripper and blogger, wrote it at a Minnesota Starbucks.
f:jurassicpark: Planned with stop-motion dinosaurs until a test by a young animator at ILM changed the industry; its stop-motion supervisor was kept on to direct the digital animals.
f:justanaccident: Former prisoners believe they have kidnapped the guard who tortured them, but none of them ever saw his face. Shot without permission in Iran by a director who had been jailed himself.
f:justiceleague: Its director left during post-production and another finished it; a four-hour cut arrived on streaming in 2021.
f:kaagazphool: India’s first widescreen film, about a director’s fall. It failed, and its maker never again credited himself as director.
f:kagemusha: Two young American admirers of its director got a Hollywood studio to fund the rest.
f:kahonapyaar: Made its director’s son a star overnight; he got 30,000 marriage proposals.
f:kalathur: The screen debut, aged six, of a future superstar.
f:kaliyamardan19: His daughter plays the child god.
f:kantara: A small Kannada film about a forest ritual dance became a national hit through word of mouth.
f:karma33: An English-language Indian film, remembered for a kiss that lasted four minutes.
f:kattabomman: Its lead won the best actor prize at an Afro-Asian festival in Cairo.
f:kellygang: The world’s first feature-length narrative film, about an Australian bushranger; only fragments survive.
f:kes: A Barnsley boy trains a kestrel; its broad Yorkshire dialogue was redubbed for American release.
f:kgf2: A Kannada-language gangster epic that out-grossed nearly every Hindi film of its year.
f:kid21: The first feature by its star: comedy and heartbreak in the same film, which audiences had not seen before.
f:kidauto: The first time audiences saw the Tramp: a man who keeps getting in front of a newsreel camera.
f:kids95: Its studio’s parent refused to release it, so its producers formed a one-off company.
f:killerofsheep: A slaughterhouse worker in Watts. A UCLA thesis film unreleased for thirty years because its music rights were never cleared.
f:killers46: The debut of a former circus acrobat.
f:killersflower: The Osage murders of the 1920s, rewritten during development to put the victims at the centre. Its composer died weeks before release.
f:killingfields: Its Academy-winning co-star, a doctor, had survived the Khmer Rouge camps himself.
f:kindhearts: A spurned heir murders his way up the line of succession; one actor plays eight members of the family standing in his way.
f:kindzadza: Two Muscovites land on a desert planet where status is marked by trouser colour; its alien slang entered Russian.
f:kingandi: Banned in Thailand for its portrayal of the king.
f:kingdombeauty: A Huangmei opera film that swept the first Asian film awards it entered.
f:kingkong: A stop-motion ape atop the world’s tallest building. It saved its studio from bankruptcy.
f:kingkong76: Its much-hyped 40-foot robot ape appears on screen for about fifteen seconds.
f:kingofcomedy: A would-be comic kidnaps a talk-show host; a flop that looks more prophetic every year.
f:kingofkings61: A remake of the 1927 epic, shot in Spain.
f:kingsspeech: Its seventy-three-year-old writer had stammered himself and waited decades for the Queen Mother’s permission.
f:kinoeye24: A manifesto as much as a film: life caught unawares, run backwards to unbake the bread.
f:kismet43: Ran for more than three years at a single Calcutta cinema, a record for decades.
f:kiss: Eighteen seconds of a stage kiss that drew some of the first calls for film censorship.
f:kisskissbang: The film that proved its troubled lead was insurable again.
f:kissmedeadly: A glowing briefcase that later films kept borrowing.
f:knifewater: Three people on a sailboat; attacked at home, nominated in Hollywood.
f:kokoda: Australia’s first Academy prize, filmed on the jungle battle front.
f:kopenick: A shoemaker in a second-hand uniform takes over a town hall; based on a real 1906 hoax.
f:kpopdemon: A girl group secretly fighting demons. Released on streaming with little fanfare, it became the service’s most-watched film ever, its songs topped the charts, and a sing-along release took a weekend at the cinema.
f:kramer: A divorce and a custody fight, starting with French toast.
f:kungfuhustle: Its landlord and landlady were played by retired martial-arts stars coaxed back to the screen.
f:kwai: The top film in America, Britain, France and West Germany. Its blacklisted writers were credited only in 1984.
f:labellenoiseuse: Four hours of a painter and his model; the hand drawing on screen is the painter Bernard Dufour’s.
f:laborer: The oldest complete Chinese film that survives, a Shanghai comedy.
f:laconfidential: Cast two unknown Australians as American cops; its director pitched it with vintage photographs.
f:ladyvanishes: Two cricket-obsessed Englishmen stole the film and got a spin-off career.
f:lagaan: Villagers play cricket against the British to avoid a tax; the third Indian film nominated for the foreign-language Oscar.
f:lahaine: Shot in colour and printed in black and white; the Prime Minister ordered a screening for his cabinet.
f:laila: Egypt’s first feature film, produced by its star.
f:lajetee: A time-travel story told almost entirely in still photographs; remade in 1995 as a Hollywood thriller.
f:lalaland: Was announced as Best Picture by mistake; the envelope was for the actress award.
f:landwithoutbread: A mock-travelogue about Spain’s poorest region, banned by the Spanish Republic.
f:lanka: A mythological spectacle and a huge hit; one actor played both the hero and the heroine.
f:lanotte: A writer and his wife drift through one day and night in Milan as their marriage quietly ends; the middle of its director’s trilogy of alienation.
f:lapointecourte55: Made at twenty-six with no film training; its editor was a young Alain Resnais.
f:larks: Bourgeois "enemies" re-educated in a scrapyard. Banned before release; it premiered in 1990 and won Berlin.
f:laroue: Its rapid-fire cutting influenced the Soviet montage directors.
f:lastcommand: A deposed general reduced to playing extras in Hollywood, restaging his own humiliation.
f:lastcrusade: The hero’s father played by the original screen spy, only twelve years older than his "son."
f:lastemperor: The first Western feature allowed to shoot inside the Forbidden City; won all nine Academy prizes it was up for.
f:lastlaugh: Told almost entirely without title cards, with a camera that moves as freely as a character.
f:lastmetro: Swept the Césars with ten prizes.
f:lastmohicans: Its lead lived in the woods, hunted and learned to load a flintlock on the run before filming.
f:lastpictureshow: A dying Texas town in black-and-white; a critic’s second feature.
f:lastrada: Won the first competitive Academy prize for a foreign-language film.
f:lasttangoinparis72: A scandal everywhere; Italy put its director on trial and stripped him of his civil rights.
f:lasttemptation: Protests, picket lines and a cinema firebombed in Paris.
f:latespring: A father and his unmarried daughter: the first of a trilogy with its star.
f:laura: A detective falls for the portrait of a murdered woman.
f:lavenderhill: A timid bank clerk plans to melt stolen gold into souvenir Eiffel Towers.
f:lawrence: A match blown out, cut to a desert sunrise. It made its two unknown leads into stars.
f:layercake: A cocaine dealer who plans to retire; its producer’s directing debut helped its star get the next Bond.
f:leavinglasvegas: Its novelist took his own life two weeks after the rights were sold.
f:lemonadejoe: A teetotal singing cowboy who sells lemonade in a Czech parody western.
f:leningradcowboys: A tundra polka band with foot-long quiffs and winkle-pickers tours America’s dive bars with a frozen bassist in a coffin; an American indie director sells them a car.
f:leopard: A Sicilian prince watches his world end; its ballroom sequence lasts nearly 45 minutes.
f:lesmis: The cast sang live on set to earpieces, not to playback.
f:lethalweapon: "I’m too old for this." Its writer was in his early twenties.
f:letmein10: The revived house of horror's first film in decades.
f:lettertothree: The unseen woman who sent the letter narrates the whole film.
f:libertyvalance: When the legend becomes fact, print the legend.
f:licoricepizza: A child actor and a photographer’s assistant ten years older drift through the San Fernando Valley in 1973.
f:lifeisbeautiful: Its star climbed over the seats to reach the stage at the Oscars.
f:lifeofbrian: When its backers pulled out, a former Beatle mortgaged his house to pay for it: "the most expensive cinema ticket ever."
f:lightasia: An Indian-German co-production about the life of the Buddha.
f:lighthouse: Shot in black and white on orthochromatic-style filters in a nearly square frame, on a Nova Scotia rock.
f:likewater: Its heroine’s emotions pour into her cooking; for years the highest-grossing foreign-language film in the US.
f:lilies: Won the first top acting prize for a Black actor.
f:limite: A plotless, dreamlike film about three people adrift in a boat; long rarely seen, now hailed as Brazil’s great silent film.
f:linshop: A small-town shopkeeper squeezed by the 1931 crisis; praised on release and denounced during the Cultural Revolution.
f:lioninwinter: Henry II and Eleanor of Aquitaine fight over the succession at Christmas; a young Welsh actor’s film debut.
f:lionking: Considered the studio’s B-picture while its A team made a Pocahontas film; songs by a British pop star.
f:littleextra: Two crooks hide out on a holiday for young adults with disabilities, played by actors with disabilities. It sold over ten million tickets, the most in France for a decade.
f:littlelordfauntler21: She played both the boy and his mother, with trick photography for their scenes together.
f:littlemermaid: Began the studio’s animation renaissance with Broadway songwriters.
f:littleshop: Shot in about two days on standing sets; a man-eating plant later became a stage musical and a remake.
f:littlestrebel: A vehicle for the biggest box-office star in America, who was seven.
f:littlevera: The first Soviet film with a sex scene, and 50 million tickets sold.
f:livesothers: Its lead had been spied on by his own wife for the Stasi.
f:livinginbondage: A straight-to-video Igbo thriller about a man who sacrifices his wife for riches; sold hundreds of thousands of tapes and started Nollywood.
f:llewyndavis: A week in the life of a folk singer going nowhere in 1961 Greenwich Village, with a cat that keeps escaping.
f:lodger: A suspected killer takes a room upstairs; the first film its director considered truly his own.
f:logan: An old, dying mutant drives a girl to the Canadian border; its star’s last turn in the role, for a while.
f:londonafter: The most sought-after lost film: the last known print burned in a studio vault fire in 1965.
f:lonewolf1: A disgraced executioner wanders Japan pushing his infant son in a weaponised cart.
f:longestday: Its producer bet his studio’s survival on it, and won.
f:longgoodfriday: Nearly cut up for TV; a former Beatle’s company rescued it.
f:longkiss: Its writer was paid a then-record $4 million for the script.
f:longlegs: Sold with cryptic codes and a star kept out of every trailer; its distributor’s biggest opening.
f:lostinthailand: Made for under five million dollars; the biggest Chinese film ever at the time.
f:lostintranslation: Its star finally agreed after a year of voicemails; nobody knows what he whispers at the end.
f:lostweekend: A frank study of alcoholism; the liquor industry reportedly offered money to keep it off screens.
f:lostworld: Stop-motion dinosaurs that pointed the way to the great ape of 1933.
f:louisianastory48: Paid for by an oil company, which got a film about a boy and a raccoon.
f:lovebug: A racing car with a mind of its own.
f:loveeterne: An opera love story that some Taipei viewers watched dozens of times; its lead was mobbed on a visit.
f:lovepop98: Shot almost entirely on consumer digital video, the camera in drinks and lockers.
f:lovers_bridge: Paris’s oldest bridge was rebuilt as a full-scale set in the south of France after permission ran out; it bankrupted two producers.
f:lovestory: "Love means never having to say you’re sorry." It rescued a studio its head of production had been told to shut down.
f:lucky17: A ninety-year-old atheist in a desert town faces the end; its star died weeks before release.
f:m31: A child killer hunted by police and criminals alike; he whistles a tune that gives him away.
f:m3gan: A killer robot doll whose dance went viral before release.
f:mabuse: A four-and-a-half-hour portrait of a master manipulator in an unstable Berlin.
f:macario: The first Mexican nominee for the foreign-language Academy prize.
f:macbeth21: One brother alone this time; shot entirely on sound stages in stark black and white.
f:macunaima: A folk hero born a grown Black man turns white in a magic spring; a tropicalist satire of Brazilian identity.
f:madamefreedom: A professor’s wife dances with other men; a scandal and a huge hit in postwar Seoul.
f:made01: The Swingers pair reunited as two boxers sent to New York on a mob errand.
f:madhumati: A reincarnation romance that has been borrowed by Bombay films ever since.
f:madmax: An emergency-room doctor’s first feature. For twenty years it held the record for profit against cost.
f:madmaxfury: Thirty years in development; shot in the Namibian desert with real vehicles, and edited by the director’s wife.
f:madnessking: Retitled from the play’s ‘George III’ because, legend says, Americans might think they had missed parts one and two.
f:maedchen: One of the first films to portray love between women sympathetically.
f:magellan: The navigator’s voyage stripped of heroics and seen partly from the colonised side. Unusually for its director, it has an international star and runs under three hours.
f:magnificentseven: The samurai film of 1954, remade as a western.
f:mahal: An early Indian ghost story with a haunting hit song.
f:makeway: An elderly couple separated by their children; it flopped, and one of Japan’s great directors may have drawn on it years later.
f:malcolmx: Its director went over budget and was bailed out by Black celebrities including Oprah Winfrey and Michael Jordan.
f:malefemale: The year’s top grosser; its star posed with a live lion.
f:maltesefalcon: A first-time director’s film that made its lead a star and helped define film noir.
f:manbitesdog: Three Belgian students film a serial killer’s documentary and slowly join in.
f:mandabi: A money order from Paris brings a Dakar man nothing but trouble; the first feature made in Wolof.
f:mandogrogu: The first film in the series in cinemas since 2019.
f:manescaped: A resistance fighter plans his escape from a Nazi prison with a spoon; based on a real escape, told with almost no music and a non-professional lead.
f:manforallseasons: Thomas More refuses to bless Henry VIII’s divorce and loses his head. Made for a modest sum with a stage actor few filmgoers knew, it won six Academy prizes.
f:manhattan: Widescreen black-and-white New York scored to Gershwin.
f:manilaclaws: A fisherman searches Manila’s slums and building sites for the girl he loves.
f:manofiron: Made during the Gdańsk shipyard strikes, with Lech Wałęsa playing himself; martial law came months later.
f:manofmarble: A film student investigates a forgotten Stalin-era bricklaying hero.
f:manoir: Often called the first horror film, with a bat that turns into the Devil.
f:manon52: The storyteller’s own four-hour film. He later expanded its backstory into the novels that became the 1986 films on your list.
f:manonspring: Shot back to back with its first half over seven months; together the costliest French production of its day.
f:manthan76: Paid for by half a million dairy farmers, two rupees each.
f:manwholaughs: Its lead’s carved grin inspired the look of a famous comic-book villain.
f:manwhowouldbeking: Two ex-soldiers make themselves gods in Kafiristan. Its director had wanted to make it since the 1950s with Bogart and Gable.
f:maqbool03: Macbeth moved to the Bombay underworld.
f:marcelino: A foundling and a talking crucifix; a huge hit across Europe and Latin America.
f:mariabraun: A woman’s rise mirrors West Germany’s economic miracle; the most commercially successful film of its director.
f:marianacandelaria: Among the Grand Prix winners at the first postwar festival on the Riviera.
f:marienbad: A man insists a woman met him last year; she insists she did not. Nobody agrees what happened.
f:marriagecircle: The first American film of a director whose light touch other filmmakers studied for decades.
f:marty: A lonely butcher from the Bronx; a television play that won both the Academy and the Riviera’s top prizes.
f:martysupreme: A 1950s table-tennis hustler; its star trained for years and sold the film himself in a marketing campaign that became its own show.
f:marypoppins: Its lead won her prize after being passed over for a rival musical the same year.
f:mash: Korean War surgeons played as Vietnam-era rebels, with overlapping dialogue; its TV spin-off ran longer than the war.
f:mask94: A rubber-faced comedian from a sketch show had three hits in one year.
f:masque: Shot in England on sets left over from a costume epic; its cinematographer later became a major director.
f:matrix: Bullet time was filmed with 120 still cameras around its star; the cast trained four months with a Hong Kong fight choreographer.
f:matteiaffair: The oil boss who died in a mysterious plane crash; a journalist researching it for the film disappeared.
f:matteroflife: A pilot who should have died argues his case before a heavenly court; heaven is in black and white, Earth in colour.
f:mayabazar: A mythological fantasy with trick effects that audiences still love; often called the greatest Telugu film.
f:mccabe: A frontier town built as the film was shot near Vancouver, scored to Leonard Cohen.
f:meanstreets: Little Italy small-timers, scored to the director’s own record collection; mostly shot in Los Angeles to save money.
f:memento: Told backwards; no distributor would take it until its financiers released it themselves.
f:memoriesmurder: The real killer was identified sixteen years later; he said he had seen the film.
f:menacesociety: Made by twin brothers aged twenty.
f:mephisto: An actor sells his soul to the Nazis for the role of Mephisto.
f:meranaamjoker: A four-hour autobiographical circus epic that nearly bankrupted its maker’s studio; reappraised as a classic.
f:metropolis: A vast, costly failure in its day. Missing footage turned up in Buenos Aires in 2008.
f:metropolitan: Made for $230,000 after its writer sold his Manhattan apartment; debutantes discuss Jane Austen.
f:michael: The singer’s nephew plays him; the last act was reshot after legal problems with the original ending.
f:midnightcowboy: The only X-rated film to win the top Academy prize. "I’m walkin’ here!"
f:midnightrun: A bounty hunter drags an embezzling mob accountant from New York to Los Angeles by every vehicle but a plane, because the accountant fears flying.
f:mikeyandnicky: One night with two old friends, one of whom has been paid to set up the other. Its director shot over a million feet of film; the studio took it away from her.
f:mildredpierce: The comeback of an actress the industry had written off.
f:milius: A portrait of the self-styled Zen anarchist who wrote the surfing, war and barbarian films of his friends.
f:millerscrossing: Written while the brothers had writer’s block; a hat blowing through a forest is the whole film in one image.
f:mindhorn: A washed-up TV detective whose robotic eye could see the truth is recruited by a real killer on the Isle of Man.
f:minecraft: Young audiences turned one shouted line into a cinema ritual, throwing popcorn and cheering.
f:miracle34th: A Christmas film its studio released in May.
f:miracleman: Made its contortionist co-star famous. Only fragments survive.
f:mirror: Memory, dream and newsreel braided around its director’s mother; his father’s poems are read by his father.
f:misery: A novelist’s number one fan rescues him and will not let him go. The hobbling scene was softened from the book.
f:missing82: An American father searches for his son after the 1973 Chilean coup; shot in Mexico.
f:mission99: Made in nineteen days for about $300,000 with no script; five bodyguards, one shopping-mall standoff where nobody moves.
f:missionimpossible: Its star produced it himself, his first film as producer; the CIA vault scene was hung on wires with pennies in his shoes for balance.
f:misterroberts: Its original director was replaced after a fight with its star.
f:moana: A reviewer coined the word “documentary” to describe it.
f:moana2: Planned as a streaming series and recut into a feature months before release.
f:moderntimes: The Tramp’s farewell and the first time audiences heard his voice, singing nonsense words.
f:momijigari: The oldest surviving Japanese film, recording two great kabuki actors of the day.
f:mommy: Shot in a square 1:1 frame that widens when its hero feels free.
f:momotaro: Japan’s first animated feature, a wartime propaganda film thought lost for decades.
f:moncleantoine: Christmas in a Quebec asbestos-mining village; regularly voted the best Canadian film.
f:mononoke: The biggest film in Japanese history until Titanic; its studio sent the American distributor a samurai sword marked ‘No cuts’.
f:monsters10: Made for under half a million dollars; its director did the effects himself on a laptop.
f:moolaade04: His last film, made at eighty-one.
f:moon: The rocket in the Moon’s eye. Pirated so widely in America that its maker earned little from his biggest hit.
f:moonlight: Three chapters of one life in Miami, made for a million and a half dollars.
f:moonman: An astronaut is accidentally left behind as the only man on the Moon when the Earth is struck by an asteroid.
f:moonraker: The spy goes to space, two years after the space opera.
f:morenaclara: A huge Spanish hit released months before the civil war.
f:morocco: In a tuxedo, its star kisses a woman: a famous moment of early sound-era daring.
f:moscowtears: Three provincial girls in 1950s Moscow; Ronald Reagan reportedly watched it before meeting Gorbachev to understand Russians.
f:motherindia: India’s top film of its era and its first nominee for the foreign-language Academy prize, which it lost by one vote.
f:motherwhore: Three and a half hours of post-1968 talk in Saint-Germain cafés.
f:moviecamera: No actors, no story, no title cards: a city day built entirely from editing. Often voted the greatest documentary.
f:mrindia: "Mogambo khush hua!" An invisibility bracelet versus a cartoon supervillain.
f:mrlawrence: A POW camp in Java with a rock star and a pop composer in the leads; the composer’s theme outlived the film.
f:mrnobody: A school videographer in a Urals town secretly records wartime propaganda coming into the classroom.
f:mrsminiver: The top film of 1942; Churchill reportedly said it was worth a fleet of battleships to the Allies.
f:mrsmith: Denounced in the Senate on release; the filibuster scene was later cited by real politicians.
f:muenchhausen: A lavish colour fantasy made for the studio’s 25th anniversary, secretly written by a banned author under a pseudonym.
f:mughaleazam: Sixteen years in the making, with a mirrored palace hall built for one song; the biggest Indian hit for fifteen years.
f:mulholland: A rejected TV pilot, finished as a film with French money; named the best film of the century by a critics’ poll.
f:mummy32: The directing debut of a famous German cinematographer.
f:muqaddar: The biggest Hindi hit of its year.
f:murderersamong: The first German film after the war, shot in the ruins of Berlin.
f:musketeers48: A dancer’s swashbuckler, and a distant ancestor of the 2023 two-part version on your list.
f:musketeers_dartagnan: Shot back to back with its sequel for about €72 million, a vast budget for French cinema, with the sword fights in long hand-held takes.
f:muthu95: It made its star famous in Japan.
f:mutiny62: A remake whose costs ballooned while its star feuded with directors; it nearly sank the studio.
f:mutinybounty: The top film of 1935; three of its stars competed against each other for the acting prize.
f:myfairlady: Its lead’s singing was dubbed; the actress who created the role on stage made a rival film instead.
f:mylaundrette: Made for television, it broke out in cinemas.
f:myleftfoot: Its lead stayed in character in a wheelchair between takes, and had crew lift him over cables.
f:myssassy: A hit across all of East Asia; remade in half a dozen countries.
f:nadodimannan: Its star directed himself and used the film to spread his party’s ideas.
f:nakedkiss: Opens with a woman beating a man with her shoe, wig flying off. A former prostitute tries to go straight in a small town that is rotten underneath.
f:nanook: The first feature documentary hit, though much of it was staged for the camera.
f:napoleon: Ends with three screens side by side; a historian spent decades restoring it.
f:narayama: In a starving mountain village the old are carried up the mountain to die at seventy.
f:nashville: Twenty-four characters, a political rally and a country-music city; the actors wrote many of their own songs.
f:naturallife: The most expensive Australian silent film.
f:nausicaa: Its success founded the studio that would make its director famous.
f:navigator: Built around a real ocean liner bought for the production.
f:nayak: A matinee idol confesses to a journalist on an overnight train; written for the Bengali screen’s biggest star.
f:nayakan: Loosely based on a Bombay dockside don; Time magazine later named it among the greatest films ever.
f:neechanagar: The first Indian film honoured at the Riviera festival; barely released at home.
f:neighbours: Live actors animated frame by frame into a parable about war.
f:network: "I’m as mad as hell." Its lead was the first posthumous acting winner.
f:nevsky: Its battle on the ice was cut to a score by a great composer; it was pulled after the 1939 pact with Germany and returned in 1941.
f:newwomen: Its story of a woman hounded by the press was echoed by its star’s own fate weeks after release.
f:nezha: The highest-grossing animated film in China until its own sequel.
f:nezha2: The highest-grossing animated film ever, and the first film to make more than $1 billion in a single market.
f:nickelboys: Shot entirely in the first person, through the eyes of its two boys.
f:nightafternight32: Her first film; asked by a hat-check girl if goodness had anything to do with the diamonds, she replied that it had nothing to do with it.
f:nightcountingyears: Villagers secretly loot a royal tomb in 1881; often voted the greatest Egyptian film.
f:nightfog: Thirty minutes on the Nazi camps, withdrawn from the Riviera competition after German diplomatic protest.
f:nightgames: A man returns with his fiancée to the castle where his mother’s decadent parties shaped his childhood. Its private festival screening was cancelled after an uproar, and it was banned in several countries.
f:nighthunter: A preacher with LOVE and HATE tattooed on his knuckles. It flopped so badly its director never directed again.
f:nightlivingdead: Made for about $114,000 by a Pittsburgh commercials company; a missing copyright notice put it straight into the public domain.
f:nightmail: The overnight mail train from London to Scotland, set to verse by a leading poet.
f:nightmarexmas: Released under an adult label because the studio feared it was too scary; now its best-selling merchandise.
f:nightmaud: A Catholic engineer and a divorcée talk through a snowbound night about Pascal’s wager, and nothing happens, gloriously.
f:nightmoves: A private eye whose own life is falling apart chases a runaway to the Florida Keys; the post-Watergate detective film.
f:nightopera: Its producer road-tested scenes on live audiences before filming.
f:nikita: A junkie is trained as an assassin; remade in Hollywood, Hong Kong and on television twice.
f:ninotchka: Advertised with a simple promise: its famously serious star laughs.
f:noahsark: Its flood scene was notorious for injuring extras and pushed the industry toward safety rules.
f:nobleza: A rural drama that was Argentina’s first big box-office hit.
f:nobody21: A mild suburban dad turns out to have a past, discovered on a city bus.
f:nobodyknows: Its fourteen-year-old lead became the youngest Best Actor winner at Cannes.
f:nocountry: Almost no score; its villain’s haircut was modelled on a 1979 photograph of a brothel customer.
f:nomadland: Most of its cast were real van-dwelling nomads playing versions of themselves.
f:nootherland: A Palestinian–Israeli collective films the demolition of villages in Masafer Yatta; it won an Oscar without finding an American distributor.
f:nope: A ranch family tries to photograph the thing in the sky; shot on large-format cameras, with night scenes filmed in daylight.
f:northwest: A crop-duster attack in an empty field and a chase across Mount Rushmore.
f:nosferatu: An unauthorised Dracula. The author’s widow sued, a court ordered every print destroyed, and the studio went bankrupt. Some prints survived.
f:nosferatu79: Released 11,000 dyed rats into the Dutch town of Delft.
f:nosotrospobres: A tear-soaked melodrama that became one of Mexico’s biggest hits.
f:notorious: A kiss split into short pieces to get around rules limiting kisses to a few seconds.
f:nouvellevague: The making of Breathless in 1959, shot in black and white in French by an American.
f:novecento: Five hours and fifteen minutes; its American distributor fought its director over the cut for a year.
f:nowavedgoodbye: A short documentary about juvenile delinquency that grew into an improvised feature, a landmark of English-Canadian film.
f:obrother: The first feature colour-graded entirely digitally; its bluegrass soundtrack sold eight million copies.
f:obsession26: A first feature from a comedy YouTuber, made for about a million dollars, that grossed more than half a billion worldwide.
f:oceans11: A casino heist by a gang of famous friends; the ancestor of the 2018 film on your list.
f:oddcouple: A neat freak moves in with a slob; the stage hit later became a long-running TV series.
f:oddmanout: A wounded Irish gunman stumbles through Belfast for one long night as everyone he meets decides what he is worth.
f:officialstory: A teacher suspects her adopted daughter was stolen from a victim of the dictatorship.
f:oklahoma: Launched a new 70mm process developed with a showman producer.
f:oldarizona: The first talking Western shot outdoors. A co-director lost an eye in an accident during the shoot.
f:oldboy: Its hallway hammer fight is one take over seventeen takes; its star ate four live octopuses.
f:oldmangun: Announced as its star’s last acting role: a gentleman bank robber who kept escaping prison.
f:oliver48: Its villain’s make-up was condemned as antisemitic and delayed the American release for three years.
f:oliver68: The last musical to win the top Academy prize for 34 years.
f:olvidados: Mexico City street children, without sentiment. Attacked at home until its Riviera prize.
f:olympia: The 1936 Berlin Olympics, with camera techniques sports broadcasting still uses; also propaganda for the regime.
f:omkara: Othello among the gangster-politicians of Uttar Pradesh.
f:oncechina: Revived the folk hero Wong Fei-hung, played in over a hundred films by Kwan Tak-hing, with Jet Li on wires.
f:onceirish: Made for about $150,000 in Dublin with two musicians who were not actors.
f:oncetimeamerica: Its American distributor cut it from 229 to 139 minutes and put it in chronological order; it flopped, and the full cut was later called a masterpiece. A telephone rings for two minutes.
f:onceuponwest: America’s most decent screen hero plays its child-killing villain. The score was written before shooting and played on set to pace the actors.
f:onearmed: The first Hong Kong film to take a million Hong Kong dollars; it made violence and male heroes the studio’s brand.
f:onebattle: A washed-up revolutionary must rescue his daughter from a colonel who hunts him. Loosely from a Pynchon novel, shot in VistaVision and ending in a car chase over rolling desert hills; its director’s most expensive film and his first Best Picture.
f:oneweek: Newlyweds assemble a kit house after someone swaps the numbers on the crates.
f:ongoldenpond: Its lead won his only Academy prize, and died five months later.
f:onlyyesterday: The biggest Japanese film of its year; its heroine picks safflowers on an organic farm.
f:ontheadamant: A day centre for adults with mental illness on a barge on the Seine.
f:onthetown: A musical that took its dancing sailors out of the studio onto real New York streets.
f:operationy: Seen by nearly seventy million people in the Soviet Union.
f:oppenheimer: A three-hour talk-heavy biography that grossed nearly a billion dollars. Shot partly on black-and-white IMAX stock made specially for it, and the bomb test was done without computer effects.
f:ordinarypeople: A movie star’s directing debut beat the boxing film for the top prizes.
f:orphee: Death rides in a black car and mirrors are doors to the underworld.
f:ossessione: An unauthorised adaptation of an American crime novel, suppressed by the Fascist authorities and often called the first neorealist film.
f:othello52: Shot over three years whenever its director could raise money, across Morocco and Italy.
f:outlaw: Swedish mountain landscapes used as a force in the drama.
f:overlanders: A wartime cattle drive across northern Australia, made by a British studio.
f:oystergirl: Launched the healthy-realism style promoted by Taiwan’s state studio.
f:paddington: A marmalade-loving bear from darkest Peru; its voice actor was replaced a month before release.
f:paddington2: For a while the best-reviewed film ever on a certain aggregator; its villain is a vain actor played by a formerly vain actor.
f:pagador: The only Brazilian film to win the Riviera’s top prize.
f:pagemadness: An avant-garde film set in an asylum, lost for 45 years until its director found it in his storehouse.
f:pakeezah: Fourteen years in the making; its star died weeks after release, and then the crowds came.
f:palmsprings: Sold at Sundance for a record by seventy cents; a time-loop romance at a desert wedding.
f:panslabyrinth: Its director gave up his salary to finish it and left a notebook of ideas in a London taxi, recovered days later.
f:paperballoons: Its director’s last film; he was drafted soon after its release.
f:papermoon: Its 10-year-old co-star became the youngest competitive Academy winner, opposite her father.
f:parasakthi: A debut courtroom speech that made its star and its writer; controversial for attacking religious hypocrisy.
f:parasite: The first non-English-language film to win Best Picture; the whole house was a set.
f:parisquidort: A scientist’s ray freezes Paris, leaving a handful of people awake in an empty city; much of it shot on the Eiffel Tower.
f:paristexas: A man walks out of the desert after four years; a peep-show booth conversation through one-way glass.
f:partie: Left unfinished when rain stopped the shoot, and released ten years later.
f:passionchrist: Self-financed by its director in Aramaic and Latin; churches bought out whole cinemas.
f:pastlives: Childhood sweethearts from Seoul meet again in New York after twenty-four years, while one of them is married. A playwright’s first film.
f:patagoniarebelde: The army’s massacre of striking farmworkers in 1921. Banned soon after release; its makers were threatened by death squads.
f:pathaan: Its star’s first lead role in over four years, and the start of his comeback year.
f:patherpanchali: Shot on weekends over three years with an untrained crew; the state government bailed it out halfway.
f:pathsglory: French soldiers court-martialled for cowardice; banned in France for nearly twenty years.
f:patriotgames: An analyst saves a royal from an IRA splinter group and becomes its target; the lead replaced Alec Baldwin in the role.
f:patton: Opens on a giant flag. Its lead refused the Academy prize, calling the ceremony a "meat parade."
f:pearl: Shot secretly in New Zealand straight after its companion film, on the same sets.
f:peepingtom: A cameraman films his victims as they die. The British press savaged it and its director’s career never recovered; decades later it was hailed as a masterpiece.
f:pegasus3: The Spring Festival hit of the year.
f:perfectdays: A Tokyo public-toilet cleaner’s days, repeated with small differences. It began as a short promotional film for the architect-designed toilets.
f:persona: A nurse and an actress who has stopped speaking; the film itself seems to burn and break.
f:phantomcarriage: Layered double exposures made its ghosts translucent; a later Swedish master said he watched it every year.
f:phantomliberty: Guests sit on toilets around a dinner table and slip off to eat alone in a tiny locked room.
f:phantommenace: People camped outside cinemas for weeks; offices lost millions to staff absences on opening day.
f:phantomopera: The unmasking scene made audiences scream; its masked-ball sequence was shot in early colour.
f:philadelphia: Its lead bought the film rights to the play to rescue her career from the “box-office poison” label, and it worked.
f:phoenix14: A disfigured camp survivor, rebuilt by surgery, is recruited by her own unknowing husband to impersonate herself. Ends on a song.
f:phoolpatthar: The top Indian film of 1966, which made its lead a star.
f:pianist: Its director, a child survivor of the Kraków ghetto, could not attend the Oscars; its star lost thirty pounds and gave up his flat and car.
f:piano: The first film by a woman to win the Palme; its eleven-year-old co-star became the second-youngest Oscar winner.
f:picnichangingrock: Schoolgirls vanish on Valentine’s Day, 1900; many viewers still believe it really happened.
f:pinkflamingos: A contest to be "the filthiest person alive," shot in Baltimore for about $12,000, with an ending nobody forgets.
f:pinkpanther: A supporting bumbling inspector stole the film and got a series of his own.
f:pinky: A story about a light-skinned Black woman passing as white, with a white actress in the lead.
f:pinocchio: The war cut off the European market and it lost money at first; re-releases turned it into a classic.
f:pinocchio22: Stop-motion, set in Mussolini’s Italy; its director had wanted to make it for fifteen years.
f:pirates1: A theme-park ride adaptation that studio executives feared their star was ruining; he based the pirate on a rock guitarist and a cartoon skunk.
f:pixote: São Paulo street children played by street children; its young lead was later killed by police.
f:planetapes: Its last shot, a ruined statue half-buried on a beach, is one of cinema’s most famous twists.
f:platoon: A veteran’s Vietnam, rejected for a decade, shot in the Philippines in 54 days after army-style boot camp for the cast.
f:player: A studio executive kills a screenwriter; it opens with an eight-minute take in which characters discuss famous long takes, and features sixty-five stars playing themselves.
f:playtime: Its director built a glass-and-steel city, nicknamed Tativille, and went bankrupt when the film failed.
f:plusone: Two single friends agree to be each other’s date for a summer of weddings.
f:policestory: Its finale sends its star sliding down a pole strung with lights through a mall, and burns his hands. The crew called it "Glass Story."
f:ponyo: Hand-drawn, all 170,000 frames; the most drawings of any Ghibli film.
f:poorthings: A dead woman revived with her unborn child’s brain discovers the world; shot on sound stages in Budapest, with painted skies.
f:porcorosso: Began as an in-flight film for Japan Airlines; a pig flying boat pilot in 1920s Italy.
f:porkys: A Canadian-financed sex comedy that became one of the most profitable films in the country’s history.
f:poseidon: An ocean liner turned upside down by a tidal wave; its producer became "the master of disaster."
f:possiblelove: Its director’s first film in eight years.
f:potemkin: The massacre on the Odessa Steps is one of the most studied sequences in film history.
f:prada2: Twenty years after the first film, the magazine is in trouble.
f:prague: A student sells his reflection to the devil: an early German art film about the double.
f:presidentsmen: The Washington Post newsroom was rebuilt in Burbank, down to its actual waste paper.
f:prettywoman: Written as a dark drama about a sex worker called 3000; the studio made it a fairy tale.
f:primer: Made for $7,000 by a former engineer who wrote, directed, starred, edited and scored it; fans draw timelines to follow it.
f:princessbride: "Hello. My name is Inigo Montoya." A modest release that video made immortal.
f:princessironfan: China’s first animated feature, made in occupied Shanghai.
f:privateeyes: Three brothers’ Cantonese comedy broke Hong Kong box-office records.
f:producers: Two crooks plan to make money on a guaranteed Broadway flop, a musical tribute to Hitler.
f:promisedland75: Three friends build a factory in 19th-century Łódź.
f:psycho: Shot cheaply with a television crew. Its star is killed a third of the way in, and audiences were barred from entering late.
f:ptu: One night in Tsim Sha Tsui searching for a lost police gun; shot on and off over two years whenever there was time.
f:publicenemy: A grapefruit to a co-star’s face made its lead a star.
f:pulpfiction: Made for $8.5 million; relaunched a disco star’s career and turned an independent distributor into a power.
f:pushpa2: For a while the highest-grossing Indian film at home.
f:pussinboots2: A late sequel in a painterly new style, about a hero who has used up eight of his nine lives.
f:pyaasa: A poet ignored in life becomes famous when thought dead.
f:qeysar: A revenge thriller that set the template for Iranian commercial cinema’s tough guys.
f:qsqt: A feuding-families romance that launched a generation of young Hindi stars.
f:quaibrumes: Poetic fatalism in a foggy port; the Vichy regime later blamed films like it for France’s defeat.
f:queenchristina: Ends on a long close-up its director told its star to play with a blank mind.
f:querelle82: Released after his death at thirty-seven.
f:quovadis: Two hours of Roman spectacle that helped establish the feature-length epic worldwide.
f:quovadis51: The top film of 1951, shot at Rome’s big studio.
f:quovadisaida: A UN translator tries to save her family inside the Srebrenica compound in July 1995.
f:ragingbull: Its lead gained about 60 pounds to play the boxer in retirement.
f:raiders: Its hero shooting the swordsman was improvised because its star had dysentery.
f:rainman: Three directors came and went before it was made.
f:raisered: A concubine in a courtyard house where lanterns mark the master’s choice; banned in China on release.
f:rambo2: Refighting Vietnam; a sitting president joked about it.
f:ran: King Lear with sons, in samurai Japan; some 1,400 suits of armour made by hand, and a real castle built only to be burned.
f:ranchogrande: Launched the singing-ranchero genre and Mexico’s golden age of film.
f:rashomon: One crime, four contradictory accounts. Its win at the Lagoon festival opened the West to Japanese film.
f:ratatouille: Its director took over eighteen months before release; the critic’s flashback was built from the crew’s own childhood memories.
f:ratcatcher: A boy in 1973 Glasgow during a bin strike; its director’s first feature, with a dream of a wheat field seen through a council-flat window.
f:realmsenses: Its film was flown to France to be developed to escape Japanese obscenity law; its director was prosecuted anyway, and acquitted.
f:rearwindow: A photographer in a wheelchair spies on his neighbours; the whole film is on one courtyard set.
f:rebecca: Its director’s first American film, and his only top-prize winner.
f:rebelcause: Released a month after its star’s death.
f:redbeard: The last of sixteen films by its director and star together.
f:redcliff: The most expensive Asian film made to that point.
f:reddawn: Soviet and Cuban paratroopers invade Colorado and high schoolers fight back; the first film released with the new PG-13 rating.
f:reddesert: Its director painted real landscapes grey for his first colour film.
f:redes: A fishermen’s strike, shot with non-actors by a future Hollywood director and a great photographer.
f:redlotus: Sparked China’s first martial-arts film craze, grew into an 18-part serial, and was later banned.
f:redoctober: A Soviet submarine captain defects; its Russian dialogue switches to English mid-sentence through a single word.
f:reds: An American communist in the Russian Revolution, with real witnesses interviewed between scenes.
f:redshoes: Its studio chief disliked it and barely released it at home; in America it played one cinema for two years and led its year in rentals.
f:redsorghum: A cinematographer’s directing debut and a young drama student’s first role; the first Chinese film to win at Berlin.
f:repentance: A dead dictator keeps being dug up. Made in Georgia in 1984 and shelved until glasnost.
f:reservoirdogs: A heist film that never shows the heist; its video-clerk director got Harvey Keitel to produce after his acting teacher’s wife passed him the script.
f:returnjedi: Shot under the fake title "Blue Harvest" to keep costs and fans at bay.
f:returnking: Won all eleven Oscars it was nominated for, tying the record.
f:revenant: Shot in natural light in freezing Alberta and Argentina; its star ate a raw bison liver.
f:rififi: Its 30-minute silent safecracking sequence was so precise that it was accused of being a burglary manual.
f:rightstuff: The Mercury astronauts; a flop partly blamed on one of them running for president that year.
f:ringu: A cursed videotape kills in seven days; its ghost climbing out of a television started a worldwide J-horror wave.
f:rio40: A day among Rio’s poor; briefly banned, it pointed the way to Cinema Novo.
f:riobravo: Made as a rebuttal to a 1952 western whose hero asks the town for help.
f:riorita: The new studio’s first big hit.
f:roadperdition: Its cinematographer died before the award; his son accepted.
f:roadtosingapore40: The first of seven road pictures; the script was offered to two other teams first.
f:roadwarrior: The punk-leather wasteland look every apocalypse since has borrowed.
f:roaringcurrents: Seen by seventeen million people, a third of South Korea.
f:robbery: About twelve minutes long, it ends with an outlaw firing straight at the audience and set the pattern for the Western.
f:robinhood: Built one of the biggest castle sets ever and more than doubled its cost in rentals.
f:robinhood38: Glowing early Technicolor and an Oscar-winning score.
f:robinhood91: Its lead kept an American accent; its power ballad topped the British chart for sixteen weeks.
f:robocop: A Dutch director who threw away the script on first reading, then saw it as a Christ story.
f:robotdreams: A dog and his robot friend in 1980s New York, with not one word of dialogue.
f:rocky: Its unknown writer refused to sell the script unless he could play the lead; shot in 28 days.
f:rockyhorror: A flop on release that became a midnight audience ritual; in continuous release longer than any film in history.
f:rogerandme: A Flint, Michigan native chases the head of General Motors after the plant closures; the most commercially successful documentary to its day.
f:rogerrabbit: The only film where the two great rival cartoon ducks and mice share the screen.
f:rojaa: The first score by a young jingle composer who would become the most successful composer in Indian history.
f:roma: A 1970–71 Mexico City childhood told through the family’s maid; its director shot it himself in 65mm black and white.
f:romanholiday: A princess escapes for a day in Rome with a reporter. Its writing prize went to a front; the blacklisted real writer was credited only decades later.
f:romeojuliet68: Cast teenagers as the lovers for the first time on screen.
f:romeopencity: Shot on scraps of film stock months after the Germans left Rome; the birth of neorealism for the world.
f:roomattop: A working-class climber in a northern town: the start of Britain’s kitchen-sink wave.
f:roomview: Florence, a kiss in a field of violets, and a naked bathing scene; a producing-directing-writing partnership lasting forty years.
f:rope: Staged to look like one continuous take, with cuts hidden in dark backs and lids.
f:rosemarysbaby: A young wife in the Dakota building suspects her neighbours want her unborn child. Produced by a showman best known for gimmick horror.
f:rosetta: Its win prompted a Belgian law on youth employment nicknamed the Rosetta Plan.
f:rouge: A 1930s courtesan’s ghost searches 1980s Hong Kong for her lover.
f:roundhay: The oldest surviving motion picture: about two seconds of a family walking in a Leeds garden.
f:roundup: Its star is a boxing cop who punches people through doors; the sequels became an annual event.
f:rover: Starring the producer’s own dog. Prints wore out so fast it had to be shot again twice.
f:rrr: Two revolutionaries, one bromance, a motorcycle thrown as a weapon; a song and dance number from it won an Oscar and the film became a cult hit in American cinemas.
f:rublev: A medieval icon painter’s silence; shelved for years by the authorities, then smuggled to the Riviera.
f:rulesgame: Booed, cut and then banned; reconstructed in 1959 and now ranked among the greatest films ever made.
f:rumblebronx: Set in New York, shot in Vancouver; broke its star in America at forty-one.
f:runlolarun: Three versions of twenty minutes; its techno score was composed by the director.
f:runningouttime: A dying thief plays a 72-hour game with a hostage negotiator; won its star his first Best Actor at the Hong Kong awards.
f:russianark: One continuous 96-minute Steadicam shot through the Hermitage with 2,000 actors, done on the fourth try.
f:ryansdaughter: Critics mauled it so badly its director did not make another film for fourteen years.
f:sacredfig: Shot in secret; its director fled Iran on foot weeks before the premiere.
f:sacrifice: The house burned in one take after the camera jammed during the first; rebuilt and burned again. Its director died months later.
f:sadie: Its star produced it herself and fought the censors to get it made.
f:safetylast: The man hanging from a clock above the street; its star climbed without two fingers lost in an earlier accident.
f:saintomer: A novelist attends the trial of a woman who left her baby on a beach; the court transcripts are used almost word for word.
f:salaambombay: Street children of Bombay, cast from the streets after workshops; profits funded a trust for them.
f:salo: Released weeks after its director’s murder, and banned in several countries for years.
f:saltburn: Flopped in cinemas, then became a sensation on streaming thanks to a handful of scandalous scenes.
f:saltearth: Made by blacklisted filmmakers with striking miners as actors; the industry refused to process or show it.
f:samourai: A silent hitman in a trench coat and fedora, alone with a caged bird. Nearly wordless for its first ten minutes; copied by crime directors from Hong Kong to Hollywood.
f:sandersoftheriver35: Its star came to regret it as colonial propaganda.
f:sanfrancisco: The top international hit of 1936, climaxing with the great earthquake.
f:sankarabharanam: A classical Carnatic singer in an age of pop; a Telugu art film that became a mass hit.
f:sanshiro: A future master’s first film, partly cut by wartime censors.
f:sansho: Children of an exiled governor sold into slavery. Its final scene on the beach is among the most moving in cinema.
f:sanssoleil: Letters from a fictional cameraman about Tokyo, Guinea-Bissau and Hitchcock’s San Francisco.
f:santa32: Mexico’s first feature with synchronised sound.
f:santovampire: A masked wrestler battles vampires; mocked on American television, loved everywhere.
f:santtukaram: The life of a poet-saint, shown at the 1937 Venice festival.
f:saragossa: Stories within stories within stories; a later rock guitarist paid for its restoration.
f:saratoga: The top film of 1937; its star died during filming and a double finished her scenes.
f:satantango: Seven hours and twelve minutes, about 150 shots, twelve sections that move like a tango.
f:saturdaynightfever: Its soundtrack became the best-selling album in history until then.
f:satya: Gave Bombay a gangster film shot in real streets and chawls; started a cycle.
f:savingryan: Its 25-minute Omaha Beach landing was shot in Ireland with 1,500 reservists; veterans’ helplines were set up for its release.
f:saw04: Shot in eighteen days for barely a million dollars; it spawned nine sequels.
f:scarface32: Its X-shaped marks foreshadow every death; censors delayed it for a year.
f:scarface83: Critics disliked it; hip-hop made it a bible. "Say hello to my little friend!"
f:scentwoman: Its lead finally won on his eighth nomination, for a blind colonel who tangoes.
f:schindler: Its director took no salary, calling it blood money; shot in black and white in Kraków, with one red coat.
f:scream: Killed its biggest star in the first twelve minutes.
f:se7en: The studio wanted a different ending; its star refused to make the film without the head in the box.
f:searchers: A veteran searches for years for his kidnapped niece, driven as much by hatred as love. Its final shot, framed by a doorway, is one of the most quoted in film.
f:secretagent: Recife, carnival week, 1977: a man on the run from the dictatorship hides out while hitmen close in. A leg turns up in a shark.
f:secreteyes: Its stadium sequence is one five-minute shot swooping from above into the crowd.
f:secretslies: Its actors were not told the full story; when the mother first meets her Black daughter, her shock was partly real.
f:selvi: From a Kyrgyz novel by Chingiz Aitmatov; a Yeşilçam weepie that still tops Turkish polls.
f:sendhelp: A downtrodden employee and her awful boss are the only survivors of a plane crash on a desert island.
f:sentimentalvalue: A famous director returns to Oslo to make a film in the family house and offers the lead to the actress daughter he abandoned; she refuses, and he casts an American star instead.
f:seopyeonje93: The first Korean film to sell a million tickets in Seoul alone.
f:sevenchances: Chased by hundreds of would-be brides, then by an avalanche of boulders.
f:sevensamurai: Villagers hire seven warriors against bandits. Remade as a western, a space film and countless team-up stories.
f:seventhseal: A knight plays chess with Death, an image parodied ever since.
f:seventhyear: A white dress, a subway grate, and one of the most reproduced images of the century.
f:sexlies: A 26-year-old’s first feature, shot in Baton Rouge in about a month; it made its distributor and launched the 1990s indie boom.
f:sexmission: Two men wake from hibernation in an all-female underground state; read at home as a satire of communism.
f:sgtyork: The top film of 1941, released months before America entered the war.
f:shadowdoubt: Often said to be its director’s own favourite: a killer uncle visits a small town.
f:shadows59: An improvised independent film funded partly by listeners of a radio show; a landmark of American independent cinema.
f:shaft: A Harlem private eye, directed by a Life photographer; its funk theme won an Academy prize and it helped keep its studio afloat.
f:shakespearelove: Beat Saving Private Ryan after an Oscar campaign so aggressive the Academy changed its rules; its supporting winner is on screen for about eight minutes.
f:shaolin36: Most of the film is training.
f:shaolinsoccer01: The biggest local hit Hong Kong had seen.
f:shaolintemple: A teenage wushu champion’s debut; tickets cost a few cents in China, where hundreds of millions saw it.
f:shawshank: A box-office disappointment with a clumsy title, it became the most-rented video of 1995 and topped audience polls for decades.
f:sheik: It set off a craze among women audiences and gave the language a new word for a seducer.
f:sherlockjr: A projectionist walks into the movie on screen. During one stunt its star fractured his neck and did not find out for years.
f:shesgottahaveit: Shot in twelve days for about $175,000; its director played the bike messenger himself.
f:shingodzilla16: The monster as government crisis: half the film is meetings, and the meetings are the thrill.
f:shining: One scene took 127 takes. "Heeere’s Johnny!" was improvised. The novelist hated it.
f:shiraz: A romance about the building of the Taj Mahal.
f:shiri: Out-grossed Titanic in Korea and announced the Korean blockbuster.
f:shoah: Nine and a half hours built entirely from testimony and the places themselves, with no archive footage; eleven years in the making.
f:shoeshine: Its special prize led to the creation of a permanent award for films not in English.
f:sholay: A "curry western" that ran for five straight years at one Bombay cinema; its bandit’s lines became catchphrases.
f:shortfilmkilling: Expanded from one episode of a ten-part TV series on the Commandments; Poland paused executions soon after.
f:shoulderarms: A trench-warfare comedy released weeks before the First World War ended.
f:showpeople: A satire of Hollywood packed with cameos by real stars.
f:shree420: Its song about a Japanese shoe and an English jacket became an anthem of the young republic.
f:shrek: Won the first Oscar for animated feature; its lead re-recorded every line in a Scottish accent after the first pass was finished.
f:sideways: Crashed American sales of merlot and lifted pinot noir.
f:sierramadre: A father won an acting prize directed by his son.
f:signcross: The top film of 1932, famous for a milk bath.
f:silenced11: Outrage over the abuse case it dramatised changed Korean law within weeks.
f:silencelambs: Only the third film to win all five top Oscars; its cannibal is on screen for about sixteen minutes.
f:silentworld: The first colour underwater feature; a documentary that won the Riviera’s top prize.
f:sindbad71: An aging seducer remembers his women and his meals in a stream of images; often voted the best Hungarian film.
f:singingfool: The top film of 1928, far ahead of the rest.
f:singinrain: A musical about the panic when Hollywood switched to sound. Its lead danced the title number with a fever.
f:singsing: A prison theatre programme, with most roles played by its own former members.
f:sinners: Twin brothers open a juke joint in 1932 Mississippi and vampires come to the door. An original story shot on IMAX film, whose director negotiated for the rights to revert to him after 25 years.
f:sissi: An Austrian empress romance that made its 17-year-old star a household name, a role she spent years escaping.
f:sixthsense: Its studio sold its $55 million back end; its twist became the most talked-about of the decade.
f:slacker: Made in Austin for $23,000, passing the camera from one oddball to the next.
f:slamdunk: The manga’s creator directed the film himself, 26 years after the comic ended.
f:slapped: The first film made entirely by the newly merged studio behind the roaring lion.
f:sleepingbeauty: The most expensive animated film to date lost money and its studio laid off most of its animators.
f:sleepingdogs: The first New Zealand feature released in the United States.
f:slumdog: Almost went straight to DVD when its first distributor shut down.
f:smile: Made for streaming, moved to cinemas after test screenings, and marketed with actors grinning in the stands of baseball games.
f:smilessummer: A romantic comedy that made its director internationally famous.
f:smokeybandit: A bootleg beer run from Texas to Georgia, directed by its star’s stuntman.
f:snakepit: Its portrayal of psychiatric wards prompted reforms in several states.
f:sneeze: An Edison assistant sneezes for the camera; one of the earliest films to be copyrighted in the United States.
f:snowwhite: Called a folly while in production; the first cel-animated feature became the biggest hit of its time.
f:socialnetwork: Its opening scene, nine pages of dialogue, took ninety-nine takes.
f:solaris: Its city of the future is a long drive through Tokyo’s expressways.
f:somelikeithot: Two musicians hide from gangsters in a women’s band; ends with one of the most famous last lines in film.
f:somm3: Three sommeliers and a historic blind tasting that humbled French wine in 1976, restaged.
f:sonic20: Redesigned after its first trailer’s human teeth horrified the internet.
f:sonsheik: Its star died weeks after the premiere, aged 31.
f:sorrytobother: An Oakland telemarketer succeeds with a white voice; the third act goes somewhere nobody expected.
f:soul20: Went straight to streaming in December 2020; its jazz was played by Jon Batiste.
f:souls: An early landmark of modern Japanese film storytelling.
f:soundoffalling: Four girls in four eras on the same farm in the Altmark, from the 1910s to now, their stories rhyming across a century. A second feature.
f:soundoffreedom: Shot in 2018 and shelved, then released through a crowdfunded studio whose pay-it-forward ticket scheme drew questions about empty seats.
f:soundofmusic: Overtook the 1939 epic as the biggest film ever, and rescued its studio from the Egyptian epic that nearly sank it.
f:spaceodyssey: A thrown bone cuts to an orbiting satellite, a jump of four million years. Its director’s only Academy prize was for the effects.
f:spaceplace: A jazz bandleader returns from Saturn to lead Black America to a new planet, via a card game with a pimp in the desert.
f:spartacus: Its star insisted on crediting its blacklisted writer by name, helping end the blacklist.
f:speed: A bus that explodes under 50 mph; a cinematographer’s debut as director.
f:speedy: Features a cameo by the most famous baseball player of the era.
f:spellbound: Its dream sequence was designed by a surrealist painter.
f:spiderman02: The first film to take $100 million in a weekend; its teaser showing a helicopter caught in a web between the Twin Towers was pulled after 9/11.
f:spiderman3: The most expensive film ever made at the time.
f:spidermanbnd: The biggest film of the year, following a hero whom nobody remembers any more.
f:spiderverse: Each frame layered comic-book halftone dots, misregistered colour and animation on twos to look drawn.
f:spinaltap: Its amplifiers go to eleven. Real rock stars reportedly failed to find it funny.
f:spiritbeehive: A girl in 1940 Castile sees the 1931 monster film and goes looking for its spirit.
f:spiritedaway: Held Japan’s box-office record for nineteen years; the first animated film to win the Golden Bear.
f:springriver: A wartime family saga that was a phenomenon in postwar China.
f:springsmalltown: Condemned as bourgeois after 1949 and nearly forgotten; now often called the greatest Chinese film.
f:spycold: A burned-out British agent is sent on one last mission into East Germany. Grey, bitter and the opposite of the gadget spy films then filling cinemas.
f:spywholovedme: Opens with a ski jump off a cliff that ends under a Union Jack parachute.
f:squawman: The first feature made in Hollywood, shot in a rented barn. The original title uses a slur, so the game renames it.
f:squidwhale: Its director’s own parents’ divorce in 1980s Park Slope; Jeff Daniels wore the director’s father’s clothes.
f:stagecoach: Rescued its lead from B-westerns and first took its director to Monument Valley.
f:stalag17: Prisoners of war hunt an informer in their barracks. Its lead thought his prize was really for an earlier film.
f:stalker: Shot twice after a year’s footage was ruined in processing. The Estonian location lay downstream of a chemical plant.
f:stanollie: The comedy duo’s last tour of British variety halls in 1953; its lead wore a full-body prosthetic suit.
f:starborn54: Its lead’s comeback. The studio cut half an hour after release; much was restored in 1983.
f:starisborn37: The first of four versions of a Hollywood story about rising and falling stars.
f:starshiptroopers: A satire of fascism mistaken for an endorsement of it.
f:starter10: A working-class first-year makes the University Challenge team in 1985; from its writer’s own novel.
f:starwars: Its director took a smaller fee in exchange for sequel and merchandising rights; the toys outearned the film.
f:steamboatbill: A house front falls on its star, who survives by standing exactly where the open window lands.
f:steamboatwillie: The first mouse cartoon released with synchronised sound.
f:stilllife: Shot among towns being demolished for the Three Gorges Dam.
f:sting: Its ragtime score, sixty years out of date for the 1930s setting, set off a Scott Joplin revival.
f:stolenkisses: Shot while its director was fighting to save the Cinémathèque’s founder from dismissal; it opens on the museum’s locked gates.
f:stoneflower: Shot on colour stock captured from Germany.
f:stopmakingsense: One man, a boombox and a guitar; a musician added each song until the stage is full. The first film with a fully digital soundtrack. And a very big suit.
f:storiesweetell: An actress investigates her own family secret, and restages home movies so well that nobody can tell which are real.
f:storyqiuju: A pregnant peasant woman seeks justice from ever-higher officials; shot partly with hidden cameras among real villagers.
f:strangelove: Nuclear annihilation as farce; its lead plays three roles and was meant to play a fourth.
f:strangerparadise: Partly shot on leftover stock from another director’s film.
f:strangerstrain: Two strangers, two murders: swap them and nobody can connect you.
f:streetangel37: Songs from Shanghai’s lower depths, made months before the Japanese invasion of the city.
f:streetcar: Its male lead’s torn T-shirt performance changed screen acting.
f:streetshame: Its director’s last film; Japan’s anti-prostitution law passed soon after.
f:strictlyballroom: Began as a student play at Australia’s national drama school.
f:strike: A debut that intercut the massacre of workers with the slaughter of cattle.
f:stripedtrip: Tigers loose on a cargo ship; the biggest Soviet hit of its year.
f:stromboli50: The affair between its director and star, both married, was denounced on the floor of the US Senate.
f:stroszek: A Berlin street musician emigrates to Wisconsin; ends with a dancing chicken.
f:struggleValley: The first film of a young actor who would become an international star, and who married his co-star.
f:sullivans: A comedy director tries to make a serious film about suffering, and learns the value of comedy.
f:summermonika: Sold abroad as an exploitation film for its nude swimming; the young French critics saw a masterpiece.
f:summerofsoul: Harlem’s 1969 music festival was filmed and then sat in a basement for fifty years.
f:summertime55: An American spinster falls for Venice and a married shopkeeper. Its lead fell into a canal for a scene and had eye trouble for life.
f:sunrise: Its lead’s award was shared across three films; this one won a prize for artistry that was never given again.
f:sunsetblvd: A forgotten silent star and her former director, played by a real forgotten silent star and her former director.
f:superfly: Its soundtrack album outgrossed the film.
f:superman78: "You’ll believe a man can fly." Its most famous star was paid millions for about twelve days’ work.
f:surrogatewoman: Its lead became the first Korean to win an acting prize at a major European festival (Venice).
f:suspense: A ten-minute thriller that splits the screen into three to show a home invasion.
f:suspiria: A ballet school run by witches, printed on one of the last Technicolor dye-transfer processes.
f:suzume: A girl and a boy turned into a three-legged chair close doors to disaster across Japan.
f:sweetback: Self-financed, partly with a loan from a TV comedian; its success showed Hollywood a Black audience it had ignored.
f:sweetdream: The oldest Korean film known to survive.
f:swissarmyman: A stranded man rides a flatulent corpse like a jet ski; festival walkouts on day one.
f:synecdoche: A theatre director builds a life-size replica of New York inside a warehouse and keeps casting himself; its writer’s directing debut, a flop that critics later ranked among the century’s best.
f:t2: The first film to cost $100 million; its liquid-metal man was the breakthrough of digital effects.
f:tabu: A silent film shot in the South Seas; its director died in a car crash days before the premiere.
f:taipeistory: Its co-star, a director friend, mortgaged his house to fund it.
f:taken08: Turned a fifty-five-year-old dramatic actor into an action star for the next fifteen years.
f:talktome: Twin YouTubers from Adelaide made their first feature about teenagers getting high on possession.
f:tampopo: A "ramen western" about a widow’s noodle shop, with food vignettes between.
f:tangerine: Shot on three iPhone 5s with anamorphic adapters on Christmas Eve in Hollywood.
f:tangobar35: His last film; he died in a plane crash weeks after it opened.
f:tar: A fictional conductor so exact that people online believed she was real.
f:taxidriver: "You talkin’ to me?" was improvised in front of a mirror.
f:templedoom: Its violence, and a small monster comedy’s, pushed the ratings board to create PG-13.
f:tencommandments: The year’s top film. Its Egyptian city set was buried in California sand dunes, where archaeologists later dug it up.
f:tencommandments56: Its director remade his own 1923 hit; it became one of the biggest films in history and a yearly television ritual.
f:tenet: Released into half-empty cinemas during the pandemic as a test of whether anyone would come.
f:terminator: Its director dreamed of a metal skeleton rising from flames while ill in Rome. "I’ll be back."
f:terratrema: Sicilian fishermen play themselves, speaking a dialect even Italians needed subtitles for.
f:testamentmabuse: Banned by the new regime before release; its director soon fled.
f:texaschainsaw: Shot in a Texas heatwave for about $140,000; far less gore on screen than audiences remember.
f:thathamiltonwoman41: Churchill's favourite film; he is said to have seen it eighty-three times.
f:theartist: A silent, black-and-white French film about Hollywood that won Hollywood’s biggest prize.
f:thebarberofsiberia98: The most expensive Russian film yet made when it opened.
f:thebatman: A three-hour detective story; its lead actor was a vampire heartthrob a decade earlier.
f:thebellboy60: Written in a week and shot in a month in a Miami Beach hotel while he was performing there.
f:thebloodofapoet32: Paid for by a viscount as a birthday present to his wife; the society friends in it walked out.
f:thechinasyndrome79: Twelve days after it opened, a real nuclear plant partly melted down in Pennsylvania.
f:theconquestofthepo12: One of his last films; a frost giant eats an explorer.
f:theconsequencesoff06: Men and women swap roles until the men revolt; a gag that read differently a century on.
f:thecow: A villager so grief-stricken at his cow’s death he becomes the cow. Banned at home, smuggled to Venice, it began the Iranian New Wave.
f:thedead87: Directed from a wheelchair with an oxygen tank; he died before it opened.
f:thedeer74: At a screening in Abadan in 1978, a cinema fire killed hundreds and helped bring down the shah.
f:theendofevangelion97: Its makers answered the fury at the series' ending with an ending more furious still.
f:thefastandthefurio01: Based on a magazine article about street racing in Queens; it became a ten-film saga.
f:thefight20: Inside the ACLU’s legal battles through the first years of the Trump administration.
f:thegangsallhere43: Features a number with sixty chorus girls waving giant bananas.
f:thehit: An informer is driven across Spain by two hitmen, and seems perfectly calm about dying; Paco de Lucía plays over the titles.
f:thehumanconditioni59: The first part of a war trilogy that runs to nine and a half hours.
f:theimaginariumofdo09: Its star died during the shoot; three friends played his part in the scenes beyond the mirror.
f:thekiller: A hitman and a cop, doves in a church, and two men pointing pistols at each other’s faces.
f:theladiesman61: Its cutaway set of a whole boarding house took two soundstages.
f:theladyfromshangha47: The studio boss cut an hour and was furious that its star's red hair had been cut and dyed blonde.
f:theland: Peasants fight a landowner over irrigation water in the 1930s.
f:thelifeofchrist06: One of the most ambitious productions of its year, with hundreds of extras on the studio lot.
f:thelmalouise: Its unknown writer wrote it in her car; a supporting cowboy became a star in a fourteen-minute role.
f:thelovers58: Prosecuted for obscenity in Ohio; the case gave a Supreme Court justice the line that he knew it when he saw it.
f:thelure: Two mermaid sisters sing in a Warsaw nightclub in the 1980s; one of them eats people.
f:themission: Jesuits among the Guaraní in 1750s South America; its oboe theme is one of the most-played pieces of film music ever written.
f:thenorthman: The Viking legend behind Hamlet, researched with historians down to the saga’s spells; lost money at the time, then found an audience at home.
f:theodyssey: The first feature shot entirely on IMAX film cameras. Its seventy-millimetre screenings sold out a year ahead of release.
f:theparty17: Seventy-one minutes in black and white: a celebration dinner for a new shadow health minister falls apart.
f:thepost: Shot and cut in under a year to answer the moment it was released into.
f:thepunchbowl44: Germany shows it on television every Christmas.
f:theraid: A Welsh director and an Indonesian silat champion shot a whole film inside one tower block.
f:thereturn03: One of its young actors drowned in the lake where it was shot, shortly after filming.
f:therewillbeblood: Its guitarist-composer’s score was ruled ineligible because it reused an earlier piece.
f:therobe: The first film in the wide anamorphic format that studios bet on to beat television. It led its year.
f:therunner: An orphan in Abadan lives in a beached tanker, sells water and bottles, and races trains and ships; its director drew on his own childhood.
f:thesouth: Its producer halted shooting before the southern half was filmed; its director never finished it.
f:thesprinklersprink95: Often called the first film comedy: a boy steps on a hose, a gardener gets soaked.
f:thesugarlandexpres74: The first theatrical feature by a twenty-seven-year-old television director.
f:thetaleoftheprince13: Eight years in the drawing, in charcoal and watercolour.
f:thething: Opened two weeks after a friendlier alien and was savaged by critics; now a horror landmark.
f:thetrial62: Shot largely in a disused Paris railway station when the sets fell through.
f:thewall83: His last film, made in exile in France after he escaped prison on leave.
f:thewhale: A comeback win for a star of 1990s adventure films.
f:thewill39: A landmark of Egyptian realism, set among ordinary Cairo families.
f:thewomen: More than a hundred speaking roles, all women.
f:thiaroye: The 1944 massacre of West African soldiers by the French army that had just demobilised them; banned in France for years.
f:thiefbagdad40: The war forced it to finish filming in America; its colour and effects won three Academy prizes.
f:thinblueline: Its re-enactments and interviews helped free a man sentenced to death for a Dallas police killing.
f:thingstocome: A future war, a new dark age and a gleaming city, written by a famous science-fiction novelist.
f:thinman: Shot in about two weeks; it spawned five sequels.
f:thinredline: Its director’s first film in twenty years; several stars were cut out entirely.
f:thirdman: Postwar Vienna in tilted frames, with a zither score and a famous speech about the cuckoo clock that its star wrote himself.
f:thirtyninesteps: The wrong-man-on-the-run template, with a memorable scene of two strangers handcuffed together.
f:thisisarmy: The top film of 1943; profits went to the army relief fund.
f:thisisnotafilm11: Shot under house arrest and smuggled abroad on a memory stick hidden in a cake.
f:thissportinglife: A rugby league player’s brutal rise; the feature debut of a critic who had led the Free Cinema movement.
f:thomascrown: A split-screen heist and a chess game played as seduction.
f:threecolorsred: Its director announced his retirement at its Cannes premiere and died two years later.
f:threeidiots: The biggest Indian film ever on release; huge in China on piracy before its official release.
f:threemenbaby: A remake of a French hit, directed by a starship’s first officer.
f:threewomen: Its director dreamed the story, woke and wrote it down; shot in the California desert, with murals by Bodhi Wind.
f:throneblood: Macbeth as a samurai; for the climax, real arrows were fired at its star.
f:thunderroad: Expanded from a one-take short: a Texas cop breaks down while dancing to Springsteen at his mother’s funeral.
f:tiffanys: A black dress, a song on a fire escape, and a caricature of a Japanese neighbour now widely condemned.
f:timbuktu: The first Mauritanian film nominated for an Oscar; jihadists ban football, so the boys play without a ball.
f:timebandits: A boy and six dwarves with a stolen map of the holes in time; its script called for someone "like Sean Connery," and they got him.
f:timewithoutpity: A father has 24 hours to prove his son innocent of murder. The first film its blacklisted director could sign with his own name in exile.
f:tindrum: A boy in Danzig decides to stop growing at three.
f:titanic: Two studios split a $200 million budget expecting disaster; it played in cinemas for nine months and became the first film to gross a billion dollars. Its director gave up his salary and back end to finish it.
f:tizoc: Its lead won an acting prize in Berlin months after dying in a plane crash.
f:tmnt90: Made with Jim Henson’s Creature Shop suits; the most successful independent film until then.
f:tobeornot: A troupe of Warsaw actors outwits the Nazis. Its female lead died in a plane crash before it opened, and some critics found its jokes too soon.
f:tokyodrifter: A yakuza film in pop-art colours; the studio told its director to stop being so strange.
f:tokyoolympiad: The government wanted a record of results; it got an artist’s film about human bodies.
f:tokyostory: Elderly parents visit their busy grown children. Topped the directors’ greatest-films poll in 2012.
f:tombstone: Its credited director took over after the writer was fired a month into shooting; its star is said to have ghost-directed much of it.
f:tomjones: A bawdy period romp with a famous eating scene; its director was so unhappy with it he considered disowning it.
f:toni: Shot on location with local non-actors, a decade before Italian neorealism.
f:tootsie: Its star fought its director throughout; the director ended up playing his agent.
f:topgun: The Navy lent jets in return for script approval, and set up recruiting tables in cinema lobbies.
